papers.title: Assessment of factors influencing the use of advance payment on building projects in Lagos, Nigeria
papers.authors: Kolawole Taoheed Bashir and Gbemisola Ajoke Akinola
papers.abstract: Advance payment has been unarguably recognized as an alternative payment method in the Nigerian building industry. This study assessed the factors influencing the use of advance payment on building projects in Lagos, Nigeria with a view to enhancing project delivery. Data pertinent to this study were obtained through questionnaire survey from a sample of one hundred and forty (146) construction firms selected through a random sampling from the total of one hundred and eighty-two (182) registered construction firms in Lagos. One hundred and thirty-two (132) completed questionnaires were retrieved and found fit for the analysis; representing 72.5% response rate. These were analysed using factor analysis. The results showed that Time related factors and Economic conditions with respective 15.34 % and 9.61% were the most significant factors influencing the use of advance payment on building projects in Lagos, Nigeria. The study concluded that ‘time related factor’ and ‘economic factors’ influenced use of advance payment on building projects than any other factors and the study recommended that the moratorium be more encouraged when advance payment is adopted on building projects for the contractors to judiciously use the advances.

papers.title: Drivers influencing the adoption of IBS in the construction industry
papers.authors: Ayodeji Oke and Olayinka Omole
papers.abstract: The 21st industry construction industry has paid more attention to making buildings smarter and more intelligent. In developed countries, their construction industry has so far adopted the principles of Intelligent Building System (IBS) to a very large extent. However, many developing countries are still lagging for differing reasons. The purpose of this paper is to identify the drivers that can and will influence the adoption of Intelligent Building Systems in the Construction industry. The study was limited to Ondo state, Nigeria. Data Collection instrument were questionnaires administered to Construction professionals (21 Architects, 62 Quantity Surveyors, 29 Builders and 64 Engineers). A total of 120 questionnaires were returned out of which 75 were deemed analysable. Data Analysis was carried out using the Mean Item score for ranking and importance levels. Results showed that the biggest drivers for the adoption of IBS are the Rapid Urbanization and Maximum security consecutively. These identified drivers should be majored upon, thereby creating a more conducive environment for IBS to thrive.

papers.title: Careers awareness among stakeholders for sustainability of built environment in Nigeria
papers.authors: Adesoye Morakinyo and Oluwaseyi A. Awodele
papers.abstract: Several inter-disciplinary careers inputs are needed to accomplish Built-Environment (BE) - a man-made space intentionally created through the use of materials of nature for the benefits of mankind. The development of those careers, which would support sustainable BE, depends on the level of awareness among relevant stakeholders. The study, therefore, assessed the level of awareness of surveying professions among career counsellors in Senior Secondary School in Lagos State, Nigeria. Quantitative approach was adopted to assess the level of awareness of surveying professions among School Counsellors. Counsellors that participated in the study were drawn through random sampling totalling 53 from the study area. Data were electronically analysed using SPSS. The findings indicate that 69.8% of the respondents do not have Quantity Surveying listed on their career advisory register. Also, 77.4% of the respondents is ignorant of the relevance of Quantity Surveying for the realisation of BE. The study concludes, among others, that relevant stakeholders are left out in awareness creation for careers in BE, especially Quantity Surveying. The study recommends expanded orientation for careers in BE among stakeholders for sustainable BE.

papers.title: Risk matrix analysis approach of marketing of construction professional services
papers.authors: Grace Kehinde Ojo and Esther Ilori Ebunoluwa
papers.abstract: Marketing is essential and it has significant impact on the success of an organization. However, risk inherent in marketing is an issue which construction professionals have not seriously dealt with. Therefore, this paper assessed the degree of risk inherent in the marketing of construction professional services with a view to enhancing service delivery. The study made use of primary data which were collected through structure questionnaire administered to respondents comprising of Architects (72), Engineers (91) and Quantity Surveyors (73) in Lagos State. Data collected were analysed using Mean Ranking, Risk Matrix Analysis (RMA) and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA). The results revealed client and other competitors relationship as the most frequently occurring risk (Risk Occurrence Index, ROI=0.83). The risk factor with the greatest impact on the marketing of construction professional services was also found to be client and other competitors’ relationship (Risk Impact Index, RII=0.78). Most of the risk factors were around the very high-risk zone; paramount among them were ‘client and other competitors’ relationship (Degree of Risk, DOR=0.65), tough competition (DOR=0.54) and professional bodies codes of ethics (DOR=0.44); hence, they constituted high marketing risk. Furthermore, there were significant differences in the views of the professionals on frequency of occurrence of some risk factors like client and other competitors’ relationship (p=0.028), tough competition (p=0.000) and professional bodies codes of ethics (DOR=0.44). Moreover, significant differences existed in their views on impact of risk factors like tough competition (p=0.002), misleading of codes of ethics (p=0.000) and technology cost escalation (p=0.025). The obtained result implies that client and other competitors had greatest risk on marketing of construction professional services. Therefore, this risk factor should be given adequate consideration so as to minimize its adverse effect on the services of the professionals in the construction industry.

papers.title: An assessment of the impact of foreign direct investment (FDI) on the Nigerian construction sector (NCS)
papers.authors: Najimu Saka
papers.abstract: Following the debt crises of the early 1980s, there was a complete shift in the economic paradigm of most developing economies as they adopted the outward looking economic model and Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) became an integral part of the new development policy. The aim of the study is to investigate the impact of FDI inflows on the Nigerian Construction Sector (CNS) output. The study used econometric methodology specifically the Vector Error Correction Model (VECM) involving series of tests and procedures including unit root, cointegration, causality and exogeneity tests as well as Forecast Error Variance Decomposition (FEVD) and the Impulse Response Functions (IRFs). Annualized time series data (TSD) on Nigeria’s CNS, FDI and Gross Domestic Product (GDP) were extracted from the United Nations Statistical Department (UNSD) database and the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) handbook on statistics. Causality and exogeneity tests estimates indicated significant FDI impact on both the CNS and the GDP. The study concluded that FDI inflow is significant for the growth of the CNS and the GDP. The study recommended for deeper social and economic reforms to facilitate increased FDI inflows to support the growth of the CNS and the GDP.

papers.title: A conceptual model for building information modelling (BIM) adoption by Nigerian construction professionals
papers.authors: Ahmad Sani Ahmad, Abdullahi Yahya Waziri and Abdullahi Nafiu Zadawa
papers.abstract: The productivity and economic benefits of BIM to the global building industry are widely acknowledged and increasingly understood. The technology to implement BIM is readily available and rapidly maturing. Yet, despite the obvious benefits of BIM technology, BIM adoption has been slower than anticipated, especially in a developing country like Nigeria. This research aimed at assessing the factors influencing BIM adoption by Nigerian construction professionals through extensive review of literatures from both Nigeria and abroad. The research developed a BIM acceptance model by extending the popular Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) developed by Davis (1989). TAM explains a potential user’s behavioural intent to use a technological innovation by suggesting that users’ motivation can be explained by three factors: Perceived Usefulness, Perceived Ease of Use and Behavioural Intention toward using the system. Findings from the study revealed that social influence, compatibility and enjoyment were identified as indicators of Perceived Usefulness. Similarly, variables such as technical support, computer self-efficacy and training were considered as positively affecting Perceived Ease of Use.

papers.title: Cost variability of educational building projects in Ondo-State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Bamidele Temitope Arijeloye Douglas Omoregie Aghimien Olusola Festus Akinradewo and Ruqayyah Titilayo Abdul-Kareem
papers.abstract: Literature has shown a wide gap between the final cost of construction and preliminary cost estimate for construction projects and this causes fear to public clients in commissioning new projects. Therefore, this research examined the cost variability between the preliminary cost estimate and the final cost of educational building projects as well as factors causing the difference between these two variables of tertiary institutional building projects in Ondo State, Nigeria. Censored method was adopted to elicit information from in-house Architects and Quantity surveyors from the Physical and planning Units of the Federal University of Technology, Akure (FUTA) and Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba -Akoko (AAUA) and the Architects and Quantity Surveyors in contracting and consulting firms that registered and partook in the completion 33 building projects of various categories from which historical cost data were also garnered. The data were analysed using Percentile and Mean item Score. The findings revealed that cost deviation in final and preliminary estimates averaged 9%. The implication of this is that clients can no longer rely absolutely on the initial cost estimates prepared by the design team. The study thus recommends strict adherence to the principle of cost control by limiting the extent of changes or variation in the original contract documents at the execution phase of the educational construction projects. The study also recommended that adequate time should be given to the design team for the preparation of drawings and specifications at the planning phase of educational construction projects. Finally, prior site investigation should be carried out before the preparation of contract documents.

papers.title: Assessing the approaches for implementing project owners’ motivation and commitment in the delivery of sustainable buildings
papers.authors: Ayokunle Olubunmi Olanipekun
papers.abstract: The concepts of the project owners’ motivation and owner commitment have been promoted as novel means of overcoming the complex delivery process and ensure efficient project delivery of sustainable building projects. However, the practical application of the concepts is not yet possible due to lack of specific approaches for their implementation. The aim of this study is to reveal the approaches for implementing the project owners’ motivation and commitment in practice to ensure successful delivery of sustainable buildings. A global overview of sustainable building in the established member countries of the World Green Building Council (WGBC) was carried out. It reveals the development of sustainable building in different countries resulting from government and private sector motivations. Thereafter, the project owners’ motivation and commitment were proposed as a synergy for ensuring successful delivery of sustainable buildings. Finally, the approaches for implementing the project owners’ motivation and commitment in practice are: modification to the existing landscape of incentivising the sustainable building practices and owner-led project management. This study suggests to project owners to embrace and embark on owner-led project management of sustainable building delivery, while a new way to design policy incentives for promoting sustainable building practices is suggested to the government.

papers.title: Preconditions for estimating building project cost in design and management contract
papers.authors: Usman Mohammed Datti, Ibrahim Ibrahim Inuwa, Nuru Gambo and Joshua Shedrack Mangvwat
papers.abstract: One of the variances of the management-oriented procurement system that is gaining prominence in Nigeria is the design and management (D&M) contract. However, its performance is marred with time and cost overruns. Hence, this study investigates the preconditions for estimating building project cost in D&M contract, with a view to attaining building project cost effectiveness in D&M contract in Bauchi town, Nigeria. The study employs exploratory and descriptive design. From a sample frame of 250 construction procurement professionals in Bauchi town, 152 were conveniently administered questionnaires. Their responses were analyzed using descriptive (percentages & frequencies) and inferential (χ2 test, ANOVA & spearman’s rank correlation) statistics. Twelve pre-requisite were assessed by respondents to be preconditions for estimating building project costs in D&M contract, and the most important ones are: scope design, employer’s requirements, contractor’s proposal, construction project management skills, entrepreneurial skills, construction estimating skills, contract execution schedule, proficiency in construction law, and proficiency in construction procurement. Moreover, the preconditions were assessed to have a strong positive relationship with project cost effectiveness. This imply that the application of the appropriate preconditions for estimating building project cost in D&M contract will contributes to attaining value for money. Hence, this study recommends: acquisition of all preconditions before estimating building project cost in D&M contract, the application of preconditions for estimating building cost of other variances of nontraditional procurement systems for better cost management, and training of construction professionals on the concept of preconditions for better project execution.

papers.title: Correlates of risk factors in joint venture projects
papers.authors: Rilwan Shuaibu Abdulrahman, Baba Adama Kolo, Ahmed Doko Ibrahim and Abdulrasheed Madugu Abdullahi
papers.abstract: The presence of risk in projects have always been a major threat to the successful delivery of construction joint venture (JV) projects. In line with the threats posed by risks, mitigating measures were developed to curtail the magnitude of damages these risks can cause. Despite the efforts by researchers to curtail the damages, JV projects continue to fail and researchers continued to report varied findings within the industry. Researchers have employed risk factors that are known to affect JV project performance with the assumption that, these factors are independent of one another. However, the independencies of these factors have not been tested, which brings the question if indeed these factors can stand as those that truly affect JV projects. Therefore, this study seeks to evaluate the relationships amongst the risk factors affecting construction JV projects. Data was collected through a close-ended questionnaire and analysed using risk criticality and the Pearson’s correlation analyses. Findings show that, risk factors within the external and internal risk categories are to a large extent suitable to be in their respective categories because the risk factors correlated positively with one another to the tune of 95% and 75% respectively while risk factors within the project risk category are not suitable to be in the same category because only 53% of the factors correlated positively with one another. Furthermore, correlation analysis between the categories (External, internal and project) of risk factors, shows a strong and positive relationship with a high level of significance, depicting the dependencies of these risk categories on one another and as such, these categorisations are not reliable. The study, however, recommends a concise validity test (content, construct and criterion-related) to be carried out, in order for the instrument to measure what it is designed to measure.\

papers.title: Assessment of stakeholder engagement in tertiary education trust fund (TETFund) construction projects
papers.authors: Muhammad Laminu Ibrahim, Yahaya Makarfi Ibrahim, Abdulazeez Abdulmumin and Aliyu Galadima Shehu
papers.abstract: The stakeholder management concept has become an important tool for steering project stakeholders towards successful project delivery. However, despite the importance of project stakeholder management as a major criterion for project success, there are no adequate research Nigeria that have actually assessed project stakeholder engagement processes in construction studies in projects. This study assesses the practice used in engaging project stakeholders in TETFUND construction projects. Semi- structured interview guide was employed to conduct interview to (10) ten selected project managers that were determined by purposive sampling. The responses were analysed using comparative content analysis. The study reveals the current practice use by consulting project management firms in engaging project stakeholders is a not properly in accordance with the guidelines stated in the literature. Therefore, there is need for proper engagement of project stakeholders throughout the phases of construction projects. This study will help project managers in capturing and meeting the various stakeholders’ needs and expectations involved in construction projects for achieving more successful project delivery.

papers.title: Training of construction professionals in supply chain management: a case of Nigerian Quantity Surveyors
papers.authors: Alexander Ejiro Omoraka, Ayodeji Emmanuel Oke and Isaac Olaniyi Aje
papers.abstract: The high level of fragmentation in the construction industry and its effect on cost and time performance calls for a more holistic strategy in managing construction works. Supply chain management (SCM) has been identified as an innovative management mode that offers a new solution for resolving problem of high fragmentation, thereby improving construction performance. However, the advantages of SCM will be inconsequential without competent personnel to oversee the process. This study therefore assessed the training of Nigerian quantity surveyors in relation to the knowledge requirements of SCM, with a view to examine their capability to function as supply chain managers. Secondary data was collected from academic curricula of Nigerian tertiary institutions through the institutions’ student handbook. The study revealed that the level of incorporation of the knowledge requirements of SCM into the quantity surveying curricula employed by various tertiary institutions in Nigeria is well above average. It was thus concluded that Nigerian quantity surveyors have the potential by virtue of their training to function as supply chain managers. The study finally recommended a need for academic institutions, and the Nigerian Institute of Quantity Surveyors (NIQS) to take into serious consideration areas such as sustainability, customer and personal service; and lean management, when reviewing the academic programme of Quantity Surveying.

papers.title: Assessment of professionals’ level of awareness of project planning processes in the Nigerian construction industry
papers.authors: Gbemisola Ajoke Akinola and Kolawole Taoheed Bashir
papers.abstract: Project planning is an essential element in the management and execution of construction projects. The knowledge of the planning processes will influence its ultimate implementation. The study therefore assesses the professionals’ level of awareness of project planning processes in the Nigerian construction industry. A total of 108 questionnaires were administered to professionals in construction firms in Lagos state. A quantitative research method was adopted. Stratified sampling technique was used. Data was obtained through the use of structured questionnaire. The collected data was analyzed using frequency and mean. The result showed that professionals have high level of awareness of the planning processes. However, it was discovered that amongst the 10 knowledge areas, project risk management has the least level of awareness followed by communication management. The study concluded that the knowledge of these planning processes will enhance project performance and hence recommends that trainings on risk and communication management should be conducted by the professional bodies for their members. Also, these planning processes should be strictly adhere to in order to improve project performance.

papers.title: Critical success factors for PPP projects in the Nigerian construction industry
papers.authors: Olusola Olatunji
papers.abstract: The use of Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) for infrastructure projects in Nigeria have increased significantly in recent years across the three level of government. This study examined the significance of critical success factors (CSFs) for PPP projects using data collected from 72 participants via an empirical questionnaire survey. The survey participants came from both the public and private sectors as well as the academia. More so, a comparative analysis with previous studies carried out in the UK and the UAE and the results reveals some similarity in some of the key factors. In the Nigeria case, CSFs such as transparent procurement process, political support, commitment of both the public and private sectors and appropriate risk allocation and strong private consortium were ranked highly by the study respondents for a successful PPP project in Nigeria. Further analysis reveals a high level of concordance among the survey participants as regards the CSFs. The findings of this study when adopted by the relevant stakeholders is expected to help in PPPs policy formulation and development as well as enhance the collaboration and manner in which partners go about PPP projects.

papers.title: Appraisal of required mentoring practices in quantity surveying firms in Nigeria
papers.authors: Kenneth Otasowie and Ayodeji Oke
papers.abstract: The paper appraised the required mentoring practices in quantity surveying firms in Nigeria with a view to providing possible practices for effective professional transition and developing leaders within the built environment. The knowledge level and adoption of mentoring concept, as well as the required mentoring practices in quantity surveying firms were assessed through a survey design. Quantity surveying firms were sampled from Abuja, the capital of Nigeria through the use of structured questionnaire. A total of one hundred and forty-nine (149) questionnaires were administered to Principals, Partners, Senior Quantity Surveyors, and Quantity Surveyors in quantity surveying firms in Abuja through personal delivery. One hundred and forty-two (142) of them returned and were found suitable for analysis, representing 95.30% effective response rate. Percentage, Mean and One-Sample t-test were used in the analysis of the data gathered. The study reveals a good knowledge of the concept of mentoring but not so much with the adoption in the respective firms. This connotes that there is a challenge with the adoption of mentoring concept in quantity surveying firms despite knowledge of the concept. Also revealed by the study. The findings show the required mentoring practices in quantity surveying firms with the recommendations to further the adoption and implementation of mentoring programs in quantity surveying firms within the country. This paper highlights the required mentoring practices in Nigerian quantity surveying firms and provides ways through which the practices can be implemented in the firms for better professional transition and development of leaders in the construction industry.

papers.title: A critical review of the responsibilities of stakeholders in building construction safety
papers.authors: Samuel Opeyemi Williams; Razali Adul Hamid; Funmilola Florence William; Hellen Omolade Obagboye and Taki Eddine Seghier
papers.abstract: It has been noticed that most of the construction sites in Nigeria experience a wide gap between safety expectation and safety realization, as some of the construction workers are faced with diverse risks and hazards. Evidently, the responsibility of the stakeholders is to ensure the safety and the wellbeing of the workers, but this has been neglected as a result of passion for minimization of cost, quality and timely delivery of the project. Although some studies have been conducted, which dwelt in the premises of accident and safety in the construction sites in Nigeria, but those studies failed to investigate the factors responsible for the low level of safety performance, particularly in relation to the construction key participants. This study found it fit to review the factors responsible for poor safety performance in relation to the construction stakeholders in Nigeria, which is yet to be filled by other studies adequately. Extensively, the past studies related to this study was systematically reviewed. it was found out that the client, consultant, and contractor have been noted for the poor and unsafe situations on the construction sites in Nigeria through failure to perform their safety duties. Besides, various ways by which the stakeholders could promote safety in the construction sites were also unearthed. Consequently, the findings revealed that, there is the need for the stakeholders to be aware of and committed to their safety responsibilities, while a model encompassing the multifarious safety roles of the stakeholders should be developed and implemented, as this will reduce the rate of accident to a minimal on the construction sites

papers.title: Effect of moral stakeholders’ participation on satisfaction with delivery of projects in Federal University Kashere
papers.authors: Inuwa Nuruddeen Mohammed, Gambo Nuru & Abdullahi Nafi’u Zadawa
papers.abstract: There is fear of the breach of duty of care which the moral stakeholders of the FUK Gombe owes the university as 54.5% of the moral stakeholders in the university are not satisfied with the infrastructure in the University. This study investigated the effect of the moral stakeholders’ participation on satisfaction with delivery of projects in the university by observing the opinion of both teaching and non-teaching staff of the university, where 368 respondents participated in the study. Proportionate random sampling technique was used to select the respondents. The study found that Moral stakeholders ‘averagely participate’ in the project delivery process in the study area (FUK, Gombe) with the mean difference of MD 2.97; CI 2.92-3.03. Moral stakeholders are “averagely satisfied” with the project delivery process in the study area (FUK, Gombe) with mean difference of MD 3.18; CI 3.08-3.28. It is recommended Clients both public and private should consider moral stakeholders’ expectation in planning, design, and delivery of their project to enhance the usability of the infrastructure.

papers.title: A comparative analysis of factors affecting contractors' mark-up decision based on selected project and organisational characteristics
papers.authors: Jonathan Zishim Danjuma, Ahmed Doko Ibrahim, and Peter Gangas Chindo
papers.abstract: The Nigerian Construction Industry (NCI) is characterised with the highest bidder mentality through a competitive bidding process. Therefore, any contractor who must remain in business within the industry must be determined and use optimal bid mark-ups low enough to win the job, at the same time high enough to provide the minimum expected profit. To help contractors decide on the optimum mark-up to insert in their bids, factors affecting contractors' mark-up decisions have been studied across the globe. However, these studies cannot be extrapolated because these studies are limited to countries/regions and the factors differ from project to project, and from one organisation to another. Therefore, the aim of this research was to appraise the factors affecting contractors' mark-up decisions in Nigeria through a comparative analysis of factors affecting contractors' mark-up decision based on selected project and organisational characteristics. A self-administered questionnaire survey was used to source information on the project and organisational characteristics considered in the study as well as to assess the extent of influence of the qualitative factors on contractors' mark-up decision. Independent sample t-test and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) were used for data analysis. The comparative analysis carried with respect to some selected project and organisational characteristics showed that the factors affecting contractors' mark-up decisions do vary from one project to another and from organisation to organisation. Competition was discovered to pose a great challenge to small-sized contractors, which can be mitigated by contractors keeping and studying the records of their potential competitors. Client-contractor relationships are also vital in the bidding decision made by contractors as it could influence the mark-up they insert in their bids.

papers.title: Problems associated with plant & equipment hiring in Ondo State Nigeria
papers.authors: Olubunmi Comfort Ade-Ojo and Joseph Aderemi Akinola
papers.abstract: The problem of Nigerian construction industry has been attributed to cost and time overrun on project delivery. The use of plant and equipment are part of several measures proposed in addressing the problem of time overrun in large construction projects. Therefore, this paper evaluates the problems associated with plant and equipment's hiring in Ondo State, Nigeria. The population for the study entails equipment hiring firms and contracting organizations. Questionnaire survey approach was used to collect data on the problems encountered in the course of letting-out/hiring plant and equipment in the study area. The data collected were analyzed using mean item score and relative importance index. The findings indicated that inefficiency of machine was the major problem associated with plant and equipment hiring for construction works while lack of technical know-how, failure to supply equipment on schedule respectively also contributed to time overrun. The study concluded that inability of hiring firms to keep and maintain plant and equipment in a working condition contributed to the problem of project delivery in Nigeria. The study recommended proper project planning and good assessment of plant and equipment to be hired by contracting organization in order to prevent time overrun.

papers.title: IFCs' Capabilities for supporting quantity take-off of building works using BESMM 4
papers.authors: Muhammad Abdullahi, Tsaku Joseph Ombugadu, Ahmed Doko Ibrahim, Yahaya Makarfi Ibrahim and Peter Gangas Chindo
papers.abstract: The Building SMART Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) data schema has been reported to be inadequate as it does not fully carter for local requirements/standards. Therefore, studies have proposed schema extensions to capture local requirements of various countries. In Nigeria, the Building and Engineering Standard Method of Measurement (BESMM 4) is currently the standard for measurement of construction works and to date an assessment of how well IFCs data schema supports the measurement of construction works using the BESMM 4 provisions is not known. This paper assessed IFC's capabilities for supporting quantity take-off of Building works using BESMM 4. Qualitative research approach based on document and content analysis was used to identify building products in the BESMM 4. Also, IFC entities that define these products were identified from IFC4-Add1 data schema. Subsequently, the extent of coverage of the identified building products by IFC4 was undertaken. A total of 28 building products were identified in the BESMM. Eighteen (18) of the building products were found to be fully supported and defined by the IFCs. However, while Six (6) products were found to be captured but partially described; four others were completely not captured and supported by the standard. The study concludes that software and BIM platform based on the current IFC4 Add 1 data schema are not adequate for quantity take-off of building works using BESMM 4 standard. Findings of this study will avail schema developers and software vendors with the information requirement for schema extensions that capture the local requirement for cost estimating in the Nigerian construction industry.

papers.title: Relationship between bill of quantities errors and construction disputes: A multivariate analysis
papers.authors: Chukwuemeka Patrick Ogbu and Vera Braiye Ebiminor
papers.abstract: Bills of Quantities (BoQs) doubtlessly remain the most preferred cost management instrument in construction procurements globally. Inadvertently, however, the potential of BoQ errors to cause construction disputes is largely ignored in literature. This study determined the sources of BoQ errors and the relationship between BoQ errors and construction disputes. Data were gathered by opinion survey of construction professionals and contractors in Edo State, Nigeria. The multivariate techniques of factor analysis, canonical correlation and logistic regression were used in the analyses. It was found that the sources of BoQ errors can be summarised as designer's competence, BoQ compiler's competence, designer's mistakes and BoQ compiler's mistakes. Apart from designer's mistakes, all the factors were found to be significantly related to the types of errors actually found in BoQs. The BoQ errors that lead to disputes were identified as inaccurate quantities, inadequate unit rates, and measuring mechanical and electrical works as provisional sums. To address professional incompetence and mistakes in the preparation of BoQs, government should insist that only drawings and BoQs that are sealed by the appropriate professionals are acceptable for the award of public contracts, and construction professionals should ensure that they carefully scrutinize works done by their junior staff before such works are sent out for use in construction procurement. The paper offers insights into the relationship between errors in BoQs and construction disputes.

papers.title: Assessment of project manager's roles in management of construction projects in Nigeria
papers.authors: Usman Sulaiman Jibril, Baba Adama Kolo, and Peter Gangas Chindo
papers.abstract: Construction organisations could have a more meaningful context through sufficient understanding of team members' roles which is now an important factor for effectiveness in teamwork. It was reported that lack of understanding of roles and responsibilities of construction practitioners (CPs) have been identified as one of the factors leading to ineffectiveness in teamwork within the construction industry. Given the existence of role conflict and ambiguity in the industry, previous researches have considered the roles of various professions and disciplines but no study has been done on the assessment of project manager's (PM) roles in management of construction projects in Nigeria. This study, therefore, assessed the PM roles in management of construction project. Project managers' roles and responsibilities in construction project management were identified from literature and used in the survey to collect data from respondents (CPs). The study adopted a quantitative approach, literature review, and finally follow a deductive approach to draw conclusion. CPs were the targeted population for this study particularly the Architects, Builders, Engineers and Quantity Surveyors. In the survey, a total of 250 questionnaires were purposely distributed to the CPs, 124 were returned which amounted to 49.6% response rate. Subsequently, the data was analysed using descriptive analysis. Findings had established that on a project where a PM is appointed, none among the roles and responsibilities of the PM identified is indicated to be fully undertaken by the PM. Also, some categories of respondents believed that a single role and responsibility can be undertaken by several professionals. Finally, the study conclude that there is a role conflict amongst construction practitioners on the role of a PM. The study recommends that CPs would need to improve on their knowledge about the specific role of PM in construction projects and the attendant responsibilities that comes with such role.

papers.title: Criteria for selection of consultants for tertiary institution construction projects in Nigeria
papers.authors: Chukwuemeka Patrick Ogbu and Monday Omogiate Imafidon
papers.abstract: Almost all tertiary institutions' new construction projects in Nigeria have consultants. In spite of this, majority of projects in these institutions underperform due to poor management as a result of flaws in the selection of consultants. This study determined the order of priority of the criteria for the selection of consultants for public tertiary institution construction projects in Edo and Delta States. First, a survey of relevant staff of the institutions and their consultants (n=58) was made and analyzed using the RII technique. Secondly, 16 randomly selected respondents to the first survey were surveyed again based on a reduced number of consultant selection criteria, and the data was analyzed using the analytical hierarchy process (AHP). In their order of decreasing importance, the criteria for selection of the consultants were grouped into four, namely: firm and firm owners characteristics, project approach, capacity to accomplish the work, and past performance. Respectively, under each of these groups, the most important sub-criteria are: public policy requirements, confidentiality and trust, perceived professional competence and experience with similar projects. This study offers tertiary institutions the priority that should be accorded construction consultant selection criteria for their projects. It also reveals to their consultants the key qualifying criteria to possess for successful bidding in the institutions. It is recommended that use of ICT and location of firm/proximity to the site should be among the criteria for the selection of construction consultants for tertiary institution projects.

papers.title: Assessment of barriers and measures to improve BIM based detailed cost estimating in quantity surveying practices
papers.authors: Solomon Olusola Babatunde, Tolulope Esther Adeleye and Adedayo Opeyemi Adekunle
papers.abstract: Globally studies on BIM abound. However, studies on the implementation of Building Information Modeling (BIM) for cost estimating are few. The purpose of this study is to identify and examine the barriers to implementation of BIM based detailed cost estimating in quantity surveying practice; and assess the measures to improve its adoption within the Nigerian quantity surveying firms. This study adopted literature review, pilot study, and questionnaire survey. The primary data were collected through questionnaire administered to both the BIM adopters and non-BIM adopters' quantity surveying firms in Lagos state, Nigeria. The data collected were analyzed using mean score, standard deviation, Mann-Whitney test, and factor analysis. The study identified 18 barriers to BIM based detailed cost estimating and identified 8 measures to improve its adoption. The relative importance of both the identified barriers and measures to improve its adoption were assessed. The Mann Whitney results showed that none (out of 18) identified barriers and one (out of 8) identified measures to promote BIM; there is no significant difference in the perception of the respondents. The factor analysis result grouped the 18 identified barriers into six major factors to include: standardization issues and resistance to change; technical change and insufficient remuneration issues; high cost of setting-up and training; weak awareness and lack of demand from key players; lack of management support and legal issues; and interoperability issues. These study findings will help to ameliorate the barriers hindering the adoption of BIM based detailed cost estimating among quantity surveyors; thereby improving the reliability of the detailed cost estimating. Moreover, these study findings will positively inform the decisions of construction stakeholders, particularly quantity surveyors to formulate strategies to adopt the full implementation of BIM in their practices.

papers.title: Indications of stress among the Quantity Surveyors
papers.authors: Olufisayo Adewumi Adedokun, Fidelis Ojuoluwa Rufus and Isaac Olaniyi Aje
papers.abstract: With recourse to the literature, today's workforce is experiencing stress in epidemic proportions as illness and absenteeism cannot be overemphasized at all levels. Therefore, this study aims at appraising the indications of stress among the Quantity Surveyors with a view to enhancing productivity while also improving stress management. In achieving this aim, 217 questionnaires were administered on the respondents. The result of the study shows that indications of stress are psychological, behavioral and physiological in nature. The top two sub factors of psychological indication of stress are emotional outbursts and depression while behavioral indications of stress include working under pressure and discontent or low morale. Moreover, muscle and joint pain and chest pain fall under physiological indications of stress. It was regarded lack of social support; lateness and miscarriage during pregnancy are less symptomatic for psychological, behavioral and physiological nature of stress respectively. Out of thirty-four (34) sub factors of indications of stress, only four (4) were significant. The significant factors are chest pain, muscle and joint pain, performance decline and lastly uncharacteristic errors or missed deadlines. The study recommends that adequate provisions for relief packages inform of having rest, exercise, leave, time off work with family and loved ones and relaxation by the employers of Quantity Surveyors in order to curb factors that could trigger stress among the employees.

papers.title: Quackery in quantity surveying practice in Nigeria: analysing the parties involved
papers.authors: Goodness Oluwatobi Bamigboye and Joshua O. Dada
papers.abstract: Quackery is regarded as fraudulent or ignorant pretender to possessing a skill or a person who pretends, professionally or publicly, to have skill, knowledge, qualification or credentials they do not possess. The menace has posed intractable challenges on professional practices, especially in quantity surveying, in Nigeria. The purpose of this paper is to identify and categorise the parties involved in quackery of quantity surveying services in Nigeria. This is with a view to enhancing quantity surveying service delivery. Quantitative survey research method was adopted for the study. Primary data were collected through the administration of structured questionnaires on client organizations, who are the beneficiary of quantity surveying services. Fifty-five client organisations were purposively selected for data collection. The elicited data were analysed using frequency and percentage distribution statistics. The findings reveal that the allied construction professionals (such as engineers, architects, builders and estate surveyors), accountants and contractors are the parties involved in the quackery of quantity surveying services. The findings have great implications on quantity surveying service delivery. The paper empirically identified parties involved in quackery of quantity surveying practice in Nigeria.

papers.title: Training adequacy of quantity surveyors in cost management of mechanical and electrical services in Nigeria
papers.authors: Victor Adetunji Arowoiya and Olusola Festus Akinradewo
papers.abstract: Training is an important aspect which deals with imparting and acquiring knowledge/skills in any profession. Every profession needs upcoming professionals to be trained to be competent to handle the work. The study aims to reveal lagging areas of training of Quantity Surveyors in cost management of Mechanical and Electrical (M&E) services so that improvement can be enhanced in those areas. Secondary Data were collected through the handbook of various academic institutions of Quantity Surveying departments in Nigeria. It was discovered that out of the fifteen (15) knowledge areas needed in cost management of M&E services only areas like quality management, risk management, preparation of bill of quantity, and installation of M&E services were not well incorporated in the curricula of some of the public tertiary institutions in Nigeria. The study concluded most knowledge areas for cost management of M&E services are well incorporated except for a few areas in some institutions. It is recommended that academic institutions and the professional body (NIQS) should take into serious consideration areas such as quality management, risk management, practical exposure to the installation of M&E services and preparing the bill of quantity when reviewing the academic program of Quantity Surveying, as these areas were not incorporated in the curricula of some of the tertiary institutions assessed.

papers.title: Traditional cost management: current practices and emerging roles for Quantity Surveyors
papers.authors: Oluwadiya Adebayo Mobolaji
papers.abstract: The lack of trust between Quantity Surveyors with other project stakeholders is impeding their ability to create value and minimize wastes in construction processes. Precisely, the adversity that exists between the client and contractor's quantity surveyors and the rest of the key stakeholders has allowed 'self-interest' to thrive to an extent that it hinders an effective cost management of construction project through collaborative efforts. Traditionally, Quantity Surveyors focused primarily on the conventional project management system, which is still based on 'project-control' that has brought a disconnection among stakeholders in design and production processes. The objective of this study is to find how an effective cost management of construction project can be achieved through collaborative efforts of the Quantity Surveyors and other stakeholders in design and production processes. The study adopted a semi-structured interview guide, where complexities in the current conventional project management system delivery model were explored. The result of interview transcript conducted with Quantity Surveyors from traditional and multi-disciplinary practices revealed some of the barriers and opportunities for the Quantity Surveyors and other construction stakeholders going into collaborative practice. The findings further revealed how lack of collaboration affects the Quantity Surveyors and their relationships with other stakeholders, which allow the issue of vested interest and power ratio to thrive among project participants and from the Quantity Surveyors perspective, a fear that collaboration would mean to collude with other parties. Despite these obstacles, particularly regarding the absence of the Quantity Surveyors in a production setting, this research has discovered that these challenges are not unbeatable and there is yet a possibility for Quantity Surveyors to interacts and particularly collaborate with the production team and overcome their relational challenges by going into a new integrated model, concept of Collaborative Working (CW). This concept can address some of the issues relating to design-estimate- redesign and lack of collaboration in costing activities which means it will not only breakdown adversarial tendencies known within the traditional cost management system, but will ensure commitments on projects, thereby allowing collaborative behaviours. The study has also discovered that leaving the right stakeholder's outside the core team (project production team) is counter-productive.

papers.title: Investigating risk management strategies adopted on road projects delivery in Osun State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Feyisetan Leo-Olagbaye and Henry A. Odeyinka
papers.abstract: Application of risk management strategies allows for effective management of expected outcome when the outcome can either be to the benefit or detriment of the decision maker. This paper therefore assessed the Risk management strategies adopted in the delivery of Road projects in Osun State with a view to ensuring construction project success. To achieve this, qualitative data were requested through interviews in order to obtain information regarding the risk management strategies adopted on road projects in the study area. 40 road projects in Osun State were identified but as it was impracticable to interview all Project Managers on all the identified road projects, a systematic random sampling approach was adopted. Whereby, 1 out of every 5 Local Government Road projects was randomly selected from the 30 Local Government Road projects, giving a total of 6 projects. In addition, 1 out of every 3 road projects completed in each Senatorial District was randomly selected, giving a total of 3 senatorial District projects. In total, 9 road projects were sampled using systematic sampling technique. Data were collated from the project managers on the selected road projects using unstructured interview approach and analysed using content analysis. The study showed that project managers use diverse risk management strategies in road projects; including reducing the possibility of risk occurrence and consequences of occurrence, risk avoidance, risk transfer, risk retention and risk sharing. Whilst they use each of these risk response strategies to varying degrees, they tend to prefer reducing the possibility of risk occurrence and consequences of occurrence. However, as these strategies may not be practicable in some situations, they then gravitate towards risk transfer through insurance or risk sharing with other stakeholders such as the client, contractor and sub-contractors. Risk retention is the one project managers are least favourably disposed to, possibly because they do not have the financial capacity to retain them or because they lack the expertise to retain them.

papers.title: Influence of construction firms' attributes on project success; the mediating role of project environment
papers.authors: Danlami Ebenezer Salla, Yakubu Gimsom Musa-Haddary, Baba Adama Kolo and Yusuf Joe Gandu
papers.abstract: Researchers have reiterated the influence of firms' attributes on project success in silos. These attributes include; market orientation, learning orientation, operations strategy, competitive intelligence and social networks. However, in addition to the non-consideration of the mediating role of project environment, the combined effect of these intrinsic attributes on construction project outcome has remain a disjointed phenomenon in extant construction management literature. In this study, a structured questionnaire was used to collect data from 373 architecture and engineering construction (AEC) professionals; Architects (67), Builders (75), Engineers (85), Civil Engineers (60), Mechanical Engineers (57), Electrical Engineers (40); and Quantity Surveyors (74). From a deductive positivist philosophical standpoint, supported by the strength of explanation and prediction, the data was analyzed using SMART PLS Version 3. The result shows fitness for an established model. It was found that 'project environment' significantly mediated the impact of intrinsic attribute of firms with varying level of impact on project success. 'Social networks' had the highest direct impact on project success. For supporting managerial actions, model selection metrics show that alternative models with promising predictive power are available. This study is limited in its reliance on empirical data from built-environment professions, based on their participation on recently completed projects. Because construction firms manifest their intrinsic characteristics during construction activities, empirical data from on-going projects may establish a more generalizable model of causality.

papers.title: Framework for effective payment for public building works in Ekiti State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Samuel Olusola Olatunji, Deji Rufus Ogunsemi, Henry Agboola Odeyinka, and Stephen O. Ogunlana
papers.abstract: In commercial contracts all over the world, payment for works, goods and services have always been a contentious issue, largely due to problems surrounding untimely payment and their consequent impact on cash flow. The problem is exacerbated in construction contracts because it is capital intensive in nature and requires that the construction contractor be paid on agreed terms in order to maintain regular cash flow and avoid insolvency. This research therefore examined the problems related to untimely payment with a view to developing a framework to facilitate effective payment so as to enhance construction project performance in Ekiti State. Primary data were collected through administration of questionnaire and interview was conducted on Clients of public projects, Consultants (Quantity Surveyors and Architects) and Contractors. Content analysis through qualitative software package called NVivo 11 version was used to examine the report on interview conducted on the problems, deficiencies and weaknesses associated with existing payment frameworks. Based on the analysis of the results was harmonised and an improved framework was developed from interpreted results. The outcome of the results based on the analysis of the data, it can be said that improved framework for effective payment developed is a critical issue that will resolve the untimely payment problem such as cost and time overruns, unnecessary claims, loss of profit, insolvency and ultimate total abandonment of the building projects. The study therefore recommends the adoption of the developed framework in this study by Government participants looking to deliver effective public project through the satisfaction of contractors.

papers.title: Business performance of trade contractors in the construction industry: assessing the factors via an unexplored approach
papers.authors: Emeka Molokwu, Andrew Ebekozien, Angeline Ngozika Chibuike Nwaole, Oluwaseun Ayobami Idowu, Godfrey Ibezimako Ogburie, and Olusola Ogunsina
papers.abstract: Studies show that trade contractors are major players in the construction industry. They reduce main contractor risk and contribute a larger portion to the construction activities. Evaluating the business performance of trade contractors is key to enhancing productivity. Studies about the business performance of trade contractors are scarce in Nigeria. Thus, the study examined the factors influencing the business performance of trade contractors and proffer measures that can be used to evaluate the business performance of trade contractors. Given the unexplored nature of trade contractors’ business performance in Delta State, Nigeria, the study adopted a concurrent type of embedded qualitative data in a quantitative mixed methods research design. In the first phase, a questionnaire survey was adopted to collect data. In the second phase, an oral interview was adopted across the state’s three senatorial zones, and saturation was achieved. Findings clustered factors influencing the business performance of trade contractors into an environmental, human resource, organisational, social relation, reputational, intellectual, financial, technological, and project factors. Trade contractors’ personalities, getting a brand, acquiring more skills, acquiring education, sourcing for finance, attending training/seminars/workshops, joining social/political groups, building reputation, and training new workers emerged as measures to improve the business performance of trade contractors. The study’s findings contribute to the literature scarcity regarding the business performance of trade contractors, especially in developing countries like Nigeria. Also, as part of the study’s implication, intending business contractors should critically study business performance evaluation operations and influencing factors before venturing into the business.

papers.title: Frameworks for developing risks interaction models in complex systems
papers.authors: Rilwan Shuaib Abdulrahman, Ahmed Doko Ibrahim, Baba Adama Kolo, Hassan Adaviriku Ahmadu, Abdulrasheed Madugu Abdullahi and Khairat Mamman Hassan
papers.abstract: Over the years, the lack of understanding of the dynamic interrelationships and interactions among several risks in large projects has remained a huge problem in the field of risk management and a major determining factor for project failure till date. Although several studies have attempted to address this issue by modelling the causalities amongst several risks at various stages of the risk management process, they are yet to model the systemicity of risks, which certainly goes beyond modelling of causality. Hence, this study proposes a conceptual framework for developing risk interaction models. A qualitative research approach was used through extensive review and content analysis of related literature on risk interactions and systems theory. The study introduced the risk management system (RMS) which provides better understanding of the dynamics within and across components of risks management process. Furthermore, the study found that complex systems theory offers deeper understanding to risk interactions than systems theory. Lastly, the frameworks developed will aid and improve understanding of the systemicity of risks as well as serve as a clear path to developing risks interactions models. This study recommends further studies to develop frameworks that will capture the risk response, monitoring and controlling phases of the risk management process.

papers.title: Investigating factors influencing bond utilization on road projects delivery in Oyo State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Olufisayo S. Ogunjimi and Adetayo Opawole
papers.abstract: The employment of bond as a performance instrument on road projects to enhance success cannot be wished away. This paper therefore assessed the factors influencing bond utilization on road projects in Oyo State with a view to enhancing road projects delivery in Nigeria at large. To achieve this, primary and secondary data were collected using questionnaire survey administered on the three (3) different stakeholders which comprises clients’ representatives; contractors’ representatives; and guarantors or sureties (i.e., insurance companies and banks) who were already involved in road projects execution in Oyo state, Nigeria. The study employed a purposive sampling technique to identify the stakeholders who had partaken in bonded road projects execution in the three senatorial districts of Oyo Central, Oyo North, and Oyo South. The study population comprised 50 clients’ representatives, 69 contractors’ representatives; and 17 guarantors (i.e., insurance companies and banks); thereby making sample size a total of 136. Quantitative information collected includes factors influencing the usage of bonds and the study identified 28 factors influencing the utilization of bonds in road projects. The study further showed the overall top five (5) ranked factors influencing the usage of bonds on road projects. These include contractor cash flow, contractor industry records, inflation factors, contractor capacity and client’s requirement with total mean values of 4.33, 4.26, 4.23, 4.18 and 4.17 correspondingly.

papers.title: Developing a framework for managing construction projects variations using blockchain-based smart contract
papers.authors: Muhammad Aliyu Yamusa, Muhammad Abdullahi, Hassan Adaviriku Ahmadu, Yahaya Makarfi Ibrahim and Muawiya Abubakar
papers.abstract: The manual approach to construction progress payment is bedevilled by many issues including inadequate cash-flow, delayed wages payment, smeared reputation of stakeholders, insufficient funds acquisition and inability to undertake future projects. This led to the adoption of blockchain-based smart contract systems. Since their adoption, the systems have been used to improve efficiency of the construction payments process. However, variations that are heavily linked to construction payment issues have been overlooked in the development of these systems. These variations are found to drastically escalate the budgeted cost and scheduled time of construction projects, and their occurrence has been noted as inevitable. This study, therefore, proposes a variations management system coupled with blockchain-based smart contract. The study reviewed literature and semi-structured interview to develop the framework. The framework three phases; variations appraisal, contingency, and variations valuation, which are connected to the blockchain ledger. This will help improve the existing variations management through data documentation, storage, accessibility, authenticity, and accessibility. Also, it will help avoid the issues of underpayment, delayed, and/or even non- payments relating to variations in construction projects.

papers.title: Causes of time overrun in real estate projects in Nigeria
papers.authors: Ayodeji Oke and Samuel Adebiyi
papers.abstract: Despite many studies and attempts to improve performance of construction projects, there are still issues with time, cost, and quality of most infrastructural developments. Most of the studies are geared towards general construction projects, which indicate the need for some specific studies. This study therefore examined the factors influencing time overrun of real estate construction projects with a view to controlling the problem of time overrun in construction projects. Data was collected through questionnaire administered to construction professionals that have participated in real estate projects. Using Mean Item Score to analyse the obtained data, payment delay by owner and financial status of the contractors are major causes of time overrun in real estate construction projects in the study area. Factor analysis was further adopted and the variables were subsequently grouped into three groups, which are proper planning of work, status of the contractor and political factor. There is therefore the need for stakeholders shouldered with the responsibility of managing and controlling real estate projects to ensure that owners of such projects make adequate payment to the contractors as at when due. This will not only ensure timely delivery of construction projects but will also aid general performance of real estate projects.

papers.title: Modelling the causal effects of hotel exogenic variables on energy cost in Abuja, Nigeria
papers.authors: Aisha Isa Shehu and Ibrahim Ibrahim Inuwa
papers.abstract: This study investigates the causal effects of hotel exogenic variables on energy cost in Abuja, Nigeria. Questionnaires were administered and data collated was analysed using PLS-SEM an inferential Method. An evaluation of the study’s measurement model shows that they are all reliable with a composite reliability value ranges of 0.770 and 0.959, all above the recommended minimum of 0.7. Moreover, the convergent validity of the measurement models revealed factor loadings of the measurement model range of 0.562 to 0.859 which were all significant. Similarly, the Average Variance Extracted (AVE) ranges between 0.536 and 0.772 above the recommended minimum of 0.5. Thus, achieving convergent validity. Using the HTMT ratio criterion the results further indicated that the highest HTMT ratio among the measurement models is between hotelier’s perception of sustainable energy management and design efficiency responsiveness with ratio of 0.652 which is below the recommended maximum conservative value of 0.85. The structural model evaluation produced a coefficient of determination (R2) value of 0.591 which demonstrates that about 59 % of the variance in hotel energy cost is explained by the studied exogenic variables collectively. The study concludes that varying degree of relationship exists between the hotel exogenic variables and thus, recommends attaching the deserved significance to the factors that assures attaining the tripartite goals of sustainability.

papers.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of codes of conduct among Quantity Surveyors in Ondo State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Samuel Olusola Olatunji, Victor Adetunji Arowoiya and Tobilola Odun Ogundijo
papers.abstract: Unethical behavior in the construction industry has been developed by the fierce competition amongst professionals, this competitive behavior among QS and participants in construction development has trigger ethical misconduct in the relationships between professionals, their clients, and the supply chain. It is against this backdrop that this study was conducted to ascertain the level of adherence to the code of ethics and the perceived effectiveness of the code of ethics in regulating the professional conduct of Quantity Surveyors in Ondo State, Nigeria. The outcome of the research serves as a cornerstone for encouraging Quantity Surveyors to comply with principles of ethics so that their obligations will be carried out in a way that meets the client's expectations and in a professional manner in the future. Quantitative research was adopted for the study and it was based on the set objectives of the study through the administration of well-structured questionnaires so that respondents can express their views based on their experience. Mean Item Score and Standard Deviation were used in ranking. It was evident from this study that the level of adherence to codes of conduct by Quantity Surveyors was due to good communication skills, discipline, honesty, and competence. Moreover, a Quality compliance program, routine checks dealing with unethical issues, education, and training were the ways to increase the level of effectiveness of the laid down rules and regulations among Quantity Surveyors in the Nigerian construction industry. It was recommended that a deliberate and concerted effort be put in place in the provision of training and education of ethics in learning institutions, by professional bodies and construction organizations. Also, quantity surveying firms, construction organizations, and regulatory bodies should ensure the full implementation of a code of ethics that will abate unethical practices in various organizations.

papers.title: Assessing the level of awareness of blockchain-based construction supply chain management (BBC-SCM) in Nigeria
papers.authors: Taofeek Tunde Okanlawon, Luqman Oyekunle Oyewobi and Richard Ajayi Jimoh
papers.abstract: Blockchain technology is one of the emerging innovative technologies in the construction sector employed to enhance supply chain management. Hence, the purpose of this paper is to assess the level of awareness of Blockchain-Based Construction Supply Chain Management (BBC-SCM) in Nigeria. The study used a quantitative methodology where structured questionnaires were distributed to professionals in Nigeria's construction sector. The snowball sampling technique was used to collect responses from 155 participants. The collected data were analysed using charts, mean item scores, and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), which was used to examine the variations in opinions of respondents. The identified variables were also assessed using Sigmund Freud’s awareness classification: unconscious, preconscious, and conscious minds. The analysis revealed that all the identified variables ranked higher than the average mean item score, with record of maintenance and operations data ranking topmost. The Sigmund Freud’s awareness classification showed that the unconscious mind had 59.35%, the preconscious mind had 10.97% and the conscious mind had 29.68%. The findings will be beneficial to both professionals and practitioners in the Nigerian construction industry in having an insight into the level of awareness of blockchain technology implementation in construction supply chain management.

papers.title: Assessment of the involvement of Quantity Surveyors in civil engineering construction project in Kano State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Asmau Mohammed Kaura and Khairat Mamman Hassan
papers.abstract: Past studies have revealed the lack of involvement of Quantity Surveyors (QS) in Civil Engineering project (CEP) in Nigeria which leads to the false notion of competence of QS in CEP and QS lack of awareness on job opportunity to explore in CEP. In view of this, the study assessed the involvement of QS in Civil Engineering construction project in Kano state with a view of improving the participation of QS in Civil Engineering projects to improve effective cost estimation in the Civil Engineering projects. The use of quantitative research approach was employed using questionnaire survey. For this purpose, 94 copies of questionnaire were administered to registered construction professionals in Kano with a response rate of 77.66%. The use of descriptive and inferential statistical methods was adopted for this research; Mean Item Score (MIS) and Spearman Rank correlation, Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and Post Hoc test were employed for data analyses with the aid of IBM SPSS 27. Findings from the study revealed that: competence of QS to value element of CE works, the most agreed upon are building material technology (MIS = 4.03) and construction technology (MIS = 3.96); It was concluded that the involvement of QS in CEP in kano is on an average and that QS are competent to value for most element of Civil Engineering. however, some gaps were identified for improvement. gaps identified includes area of transport engineering, geotechnical engineering, water resources & irrigation engineering and hydraulics. It was therefore recommended that QS fill the gap and acquire basic skills for the element as you can’t measure what you don’t know and to fully participate in CEP and for QS to end the conservative era and diversify as their involvement equals effective estimation of CEP.

papers.title: An Exploratory Factor Analysis of the Causes, Effects, and Survival Strategies for Construction Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Abuja
papers.authors: Luqman Oyekunle Oyewobi, Taofeek Tunde Okanlawon, Ibrahim Inyas Adamu and Richard Ajayi Jimoh
papers.abstract: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) are essential catalysts for economic development, employment generation, and innovation globally, particularly within the construction sector. However, these enterprises encounter substantial challenges, including economic recessions, variable demand, restricted access to capital, and the intricacies of a competitive market. Hence, the purpose of this study is to assess the survival strategies being used by the Nigerian construction industry SMEs which was achieved by examining the causes of their failure, the effects of the failure on their existence, and the strategies that can be deployed to mitigate the failure. The study adopted a survey design by administering questionnaires to 142 registered SMEs who were actively involved in the delivery of infrastructure assets in Abuja, Nigeria. Out of 142 administered questionnaires, only 105 were returned and considered valid for the analyses presented in this paper. The data gathered were then analysed using mean item scores and factor analysis. The findings from the study revealed that poor communication and the drop in the confidence of the owner of SMEs due to factors like occupational stress and psychological strain are top major causes of failure of SMEs. Furthermore, lack of improvement in skills by the owners in expansion is one of the effects of failure among the SMEs studied. Minimizing staff redundancies are a major technique employed to overcome the failure of the construction SMEs, forming partnership with large construction firms and diversifying into different non-construction related business are seen as the most relevant strategy to be used by the SMEs owners to ensure survival. The findings provided valuable lessons to SMEs to prepare for volatile construction market conditions considering the Covid – 19 pandemic the country is facing. The paper also extended the debate on SMEs growth constraints with regards to survival strategy.

papers.title: Evaluation of Drivers for the Implementation of Automation in Quantity Surveying Firms in Lagos State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Ogobuchi Oka Nkama, Ibukun Oluwadara Famakin and Ayodeji Emmanuel Oke
papers.abstract: The construction industry demands active construction organisations, efficient construction processes and innovative construction techniques to effectively compete under increasing globalisation, market competition and technological advancements in the twenty-first century. Therefore, this research work evaluates the drivers to the implementation of automation in Quantity Surveying Firms (QSFs) in Lagos state, Nigeria. Data was obtained through the administration of a well-structured questionnaire to QSFs irrespective of their organisational affliction (i.e. consulting or contracting firm) with a response rate of 85.96%. The data obtained was analyzed using the Mean Item Score (MIS) and Factor analysis. The research findings reveal that information and communication technology (ICT), effective communication channel, good working collaboration and availability of plants/equipment/machineries/technology are the most significant drivers to the implementation of automation in QSFs in Lagos state. The factor analysis of the study revealed four (4) key components, including human, operation, management, and Data/ICT drivers to the implementation of automation. It is therefore recommended that construction firms' workers' need mechatronic training, qualifications, effective and sustainable public enlightenment programme to sensitize the residents, developers and other stakeholders in the construction industry on the need for automation, as this would implicitly create a conducive and harmonious environment for living, working and recreating.

papers.title: Knowledge Management among Indigenous Construction Firms in Nigeria: Barriers and Strategies for improvement
papers.authors: Emmanuel Tayo Adu, Adewale Segun Alabi & Oluwadamilola Ajoke Alabi
papers.abstract: Despite the clear benefits of knowledge management (KM) in enhancing project efficiency and competitiveness, indigenous construction firms in Nigeria face significant challenges in adopting modern KM systems. The study aims to bridge the gap between traditional and modern knowledge systems, with the view to enhancing KM practices within indigenous construction firms. The objectives of the study are to assess the barriers to modern KM adoption and propose actionable strategies for its implementation among indigenous construction professionals in Nigeria. A questionnaire survey was developed for data collection, based on a thorough literature review that identified 34 barriers and 26 strategies for the implementation of modern KM among indigenous construction professionals. A stratified random sampling technique was adopted to ensure adequate representation of various professional groups within indigenous contracting firms. Mean score and Kruskal-Wallis Test were employed for data analysis. The top five barriers to adoption of modern KM among indigenous construction firms are a lack of leadership commitment, limited awareness of KM benefits, an unclear organizational vision for KM, budgetary constraints, and inadequate IT infrastructure. Dominant strategies for overcoming KM adoption barriers include securing strong support from top management to prioritize KM initiatives, investing in relevant KM tools and technologies, and ensuring the integration of KM systems across all levels of the organization. The research emphasizes the critical importance of integrating traditional knowledge with modern KM systems. By leveraging local expertise alongside contemporary KM practices, indigenous construction firms can enhance operational efficiency and strengthen their competitive position in the market.

papers.title: Exploring Design-Bid-Build Quarterback Narratives in Nigerian Construction Industry
papers.authors: Danlami Ebenezer Salla, Shehu Ahmadu Bustani, Alhassan Dahiru and Benedict Yashim Bakut
papers.abstract: The traditional procurement route otherwise known as the Design Bid and Build (DBB) has been widely adopted, generously acknowledged, yet, loosely defined in terms of its quarterback narrative. Although previous studies have identified the unique attributes of the DBB, a gap exists in literature on the relevance of such attributes as prioritized by practitioners. The present study aims at exploring DBB quarterback narrative as perceived by built-environment professionals in Nigerian construction industry. As a proxy for appreciating the sentiment of professionals on DBB project delivery, respondents to the questionnaire comprising of 140 randomly selected professionals in Nigeria were asked to rank 50 basic features of the DBB on a 5-point Likert scale. With the aid of SPSS version 24, data was analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. The result shows that the DBB method is perceived differently by Nigerian professionals according to their stakes on construction projects. Perception on the 'potentials for guaranteeing cost certainty to client' is still widely held justification for DBB preference amongst Nigerian construction professionals. DBB remains a common project delivery route in Nigerian construction projects, but may be inadequate for meeting up with the diverse needs of the Nigerian construction market. The present study complements previous studies in prioritizing professionals' preferences on the DBB narratives. Policies on public construction projects can leverage on the views of the professionals towards accommodating changes in the traditional procurement route by incorporating the quarterback narrative(s) for improved construction project delivery.

papers.title: Service quality of Quantity Surveyors in oil and gas projects in Nigeria
papers.authors: Dele S. Kadiri and Bukola T. Fashola
papers.abstract: The Nigerian Oil and Gas Industry Content Development Act (2010) was enacted to promote increased Nigerian participation in the industry. However, extant literature indicates the low involvement of Quantity Surveyors in oil and gas projects in Nigeria.
