It is a well-known fact that poor quality service results in customer dissatisfaction which not only translates to customer attrition but also unwillingness to recommend the service provider to others. The question could be asked if this low involvement is due to perceived poor quality service rendered by Quantity Surveyors on oil and gas projects. This paper hence investigated the service quality of Quantity Surveyors in oil and gas projects in Nigeria using a 10-dimentional model which is recommended to transcend all services. A structured questionnaire was used to ascertain feedback on the expectations and perceptions of the services rendered by Quantity Surveyors on oil and gas projects from 16 out of 31 oil and gas client organizations operating in Nigeria. The data collected were analysed using mean score and ANOVA. Findings from this paper indicated that out of the 10 quality dimensions investigated, clients' perceptions exceeded expectations in only one (Tangibles) dimension. This paper hence concluded that the service quality of Quantity Surveyors in the oil and gas sector of Nigeria is largely unsatisfactory.

papers.title: Impact of transformational and transactional leadership styles on employee commitment: the mediating effect of job satisfaction
papers.authors: Luqman Oyekunle Oyewobi, Taofeek Tunde Okanlawon, Ibrahim Inyas Adamu and Richard Ajayi Jimoh
papers.abstract: Employee commitment is a vital determinant of organizational success, affecting productivity, retention, and overall performance. In the current competitive business landscape, organizations strive to improve commitment levels through the implementation of effective leadership styles. However, transformational and transactional leadership styles have garnered considerable attention among the various leadership paradigms due to their unique methods of motivating and managing employees. Thus, the purpose of this study is to examine how job satisfaction affects the relationship between transformational and transactional leadership styles and employee commitment among quantity surveyors in private consulting firms in Nigeria. The study used quantitative methods to collect cross-sectional data from 127 practicing quantity surveying firms (QSFs) in Abuja. A total of 76 valid questionnaires were returned out of a sample of 127. This is a response rate of almost 60%, and the study's hypotheses were tested using Partial Least Square Structural Equation Modeling. According to the findings, transformational and transactional leadership styles have a direct and strong positive link with the employee commitment of quantity surveyors in the Nigerian private quantity surveying consulting organizations. Furthermore, the findings demonstrate that job satisfaction has competitive partial mediation on the relationship between both leadership styles and employee commitment. This study adds to the body of knowledge by providing more evidence on the relationship between transformational and transactional leadership styles and employee commitment among quantity surveyors in private consulting firms in Nigeria. It also reveals that, in the context of a private business, job satisfaction partially mediates the influence of both leadership styles on employee commitment.

papers.title: Evaluation of Quantity Surveyor's Involvement in Engineering Projects Delivery in Ondo State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Bamidele Temitope Arijeloye, Lekan Damilola Ojo and Dorcas Titilayo Moyanga
papers.abstract: Construction project delivery involves participation of various construction professionals, artisans, and government bodies. This study evaluates Quantity Surveyor (QS) involvement in engineering project delivery in Ondo state, Nigeria. Survey design was adopted for this study using structured questionnaire. Seventy-five (75) copies of questionnaires were administered, out of which 50 were returned and was found fit for analysis. Frequency and percentile were used to analyze background information of the respondents while mean score was used to analyze involvement of QS at feasibility stage of engineering projects and responsibilities of QS at construction stage of engineering projects. The study shows that QS are well involved in during the Feasibility stages of engineering project and this is beneficial to all construction professionals and client. Also QS responsibilities at construction stage was assessed and the study revealed that QS services are needed for prompt delivery of construction project to budgeted cost in engineering construction projects. The study advocated a change in general perception that only the engineers can manage engineering projects, QS should always be included in civil engineering projects so that construction industry will benefit from the dynamism of the quantity surveying profession.

papers.title: Responsiveness of Contractors' Bids for Public Construction Projects in Nigeria
papers.authors: Nofiu Abiodun Musa, Abdulkadir Shehu Rasheed and Victoria Tolulope Oladele
papers.abstract: Many construction firms in Nigeria are folding-up due to unsuccessful tendering consequent upon noncompliance with the bid solicitation requirements. Reversal of this ugly trend is imperative for the country to achieve sustainable development in construction. Hence, the main aim of this study was to examine the tenders submitted by contractors in competition for public construction projects in Nigeria with a view to determining their compliance with the bids' solicitation notice requirements – responsiveness and the deficient parts of the tenders needing the bidders' attention for compliance. Towards this end, primary data were collected through two sets of questionnaires. The first set were administered through email (due to ravaging covid-19 pandemic) on chief executive officers/managing directors (CEO/MD) of a sample of sixty-three (63) construction companies selected randomly from eighty-five (85) members of the full membership category in the register of Federation of Construction Industry (FOCI) (FOCI, 2019). The second set were administered on the principal partners of a sample of one hundred and eighteen (118) quantity surveying firms that were responsible for the evaluation of the contractors' tenders submitted in competition for construction projects across the country. The quantity surveying firms were selected from three-hundred and eighty-eight (388) members on the list of registered firms in the register of Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria (QSRBN) (QSRBN, 2019) using systematic random sampling technique. The data obtained were subjected to both descriptive and inferential statistics such as means, percentages, mean item score (MIS) and t-test. IBM Statistical Package for Social Sciences (SPSS) version 25 was employed for the analysis. The results revealed that the responsiveness of tenders submitted by the contractors in competition for construction works in Nigeria are 36% corporately (as business entity) and 38% competitively among other contractors. The result further revealed that the tenders are not entirely compliant with the clients' tenders' requirements due to frequent violation of bid submittal requirements (MIS = 4.3), payment of VAT and tax (MIS = 4.1), compliance with staff retirement scheme (MIS = 3.9), signing of price bid form and price schedule (MIS= 3.6) and eligibility requirements (MIS= 3.6). The paper concluded that the submitted tenders are poorly responsive to the tender requirements of the clients.

papers.title: Benchmarking hotel energy performance in Abuja, Nigeria using established best practice metrics
papers.authors: A. I. Shehu and Ibrahim I. Inuwa
papers.abstract: Forty percent of Nigeria's hotel business revenues is spent on energy due to the dwindling national energy system. This calls for the exploration of the sustainability of Nigeria's hotels energy consumption. Thus, this study assesses hotel energy performance in Abuja, Nigeria using best practice benchmarks. The study employed literature review, structured interview and archival materials to collate data. The data was analysed using descriptive statistics and documented best practice benchmarks. Results revealed that the amount of energy consumed varies between different hotel typology. All the studied hotels sourced 62.56%, 36.34% and 1.10% of their energies from electricity, diesel, and LPG respectively; none is using renewable energy. The findings indicated that the EUIe of the sampled hotels were 303.51kWh/m², 227.54kWh/m², 246.91kWh/m² and 198.74kWh/m² respectively. This connotes that the energy use intensity indices for electricity of the hotels fall within poor performance benchmarks of >150kWh/m² for 5 and 4-star hotels and >140, >120kWh/m² for 3 and 2-star hotels respectively. The hotels EUIf were 161.47 kWh/m², 235.63kWh/m², 152.34 kWh/m², and 136.28 kWh/m² respectively revealing that fossil fuel consumption is accordingly of good performance falling within good performance benchmarks of <300 for 5 and 4-star hotels and <260, >240kWh/m² for 3 and 2-star hotels respectively. Based on these outcomes, it is apparent that Nigeria's hotels main source of energy consumption is not sustainable and as such increased their operating costs. This study recommended that hotels in Nigeria should appropriately utilize renewable energy sources in their energy use mix in line with best practice.

papers.title: Perception of professional women on breaking the glass ceiling in the Nigerian construction industry
papers.authors: Fatima Muhammad Bello, Kulomri Jipato Adogbo and Joy Joshua Maina
papers.abstract: Professional women in the construction industry face barriers that challenge their career progression which could lead to underachievement or women could adopt success strategies to deal with these barriers and experience career progression. This study assessed the perceptions of women professionals regarding breaking the glass ceiling in the Nigerian construction industry. This study adopted a quantitative approach using a structured questionnaire which was administered electronically. In total, 120 valid responses were included in the analyses. Data were analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics (means, percentages, and ANOVA and are presented in tables). Findings from the study revealed that women who have broken through the glass ceiling are focused on their careers and ensure that people recognise their qualifications at work and are deliberate about continuous professional development programmes. The study therefore concludes that a glass ceiling exists and that women have broken through this barrier in various workplaces, and there exist strategies for women to advance successfully in the Nigerian Construction Industry. It is recommended that women focus on their careers and be deliberate about continuous learning, taking advantage of every opportunity for work that arises in their offices.

papers.title: Effect of uncertainty factors on the duration of renovation projects
papers.authors: Dandago Abdulmalik Abba, Ibrahim Maryam Namadina, Yamusa Muhammad Aliyu, and Lawal Haruna Saidu
papers.abstract: The duration of a construction project is crucial for evaluating its overall performance. Incorrect estimation of project duration can lead to poor performance and failure to achieve project objectives. Efforts have been made to identify factors affecting construction duration, but concerns about uncertainties in construction activities persist. Despite efforts to assess uncertainties affecting construction duration, insufficient effort has been made for renovation projects, which are established to be more challenging and characterized by inaccurate scope of work. This paper aims to assess uncertainty factors affecting the duration of different types of renovation works. A quantitative approach was used, collecting data from a questionnaire on 45 uncertainty factors affecting duration. Data collected was analysed using Mean score, Normality test, Kruskal-Wallis test, and Mann-Whitney U-test. The results revealed Inflation rate, financial problems (limitations on the provision of credit), delays in payment, Weather, and Late issuing of approval documents as the top five uncertainty factors which affect the duration of building renovation projects the most. It also concluded that project type does not significantly affect how the factors influence the duration, while the type of funding significantly affects how the uncertainties influence the project duration. The study implied that a contractor should have a consistent cash flow and reliable funding source to avoid delay in the duration of renovation works.

papers.title: Modelling construction durations for building projects in Nigeria
papers.authors: Comfort Olubunmi Ade-Ojo and Emmanuel Opeyemi Olorundare
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of construction project duration is a significant challenge, particularly when considering various delay factors. Although numerous models have been developed to identify causes of duration delays on construction sites, their applicability is often limited to specific regions or countries. This study aimed to create a construction time prediction model tailored to the Nigerian construction industry. A comprehensive review of past literature identified key quantitative variables influencing construction time prediction. Data normalization was achieved through logarithmic transformation. Using Statistical Package for Social Science (SPSS) version 26, a multiple regression analysis was conducted to examine the relationship between independent variables (gross floor area, number of floors, and floor height) and the dependent variable (construction time). The analysis considered data from 30 public residential building projects undertaken by the Federal Ministry of Defense in Abuja between 2016 and 2020. The results showed a strong correlation, with R2 = 0.637. The result implies that the independent variables explain 64% of the variance in the prediction model. This model can be a valuable tool for project managers and contractors to predict construction time and facilitate effective planning. Future research is recommended to explore additional statistical techniques further to improve the accuracy of project construction duration predictions”.

papers.title: Application of whole life costing in Nigerian construction industry: A case of public tertiary education building projects in Yobe State
papers.authors: Bashir Abdullahi, Musa Mohammed Mukhtar and Nuru Gambo
papers.abstract: The construction industry has largely acknowledged the benefits that whole life cost based decision-making can bring to the design and operation of building assets. To achieve a successful building project, all costs incurred over the whole life span must be evaluated. However, despite the benefits of WLC practices its implementation in the Nigerian construction industry was low. The aim of this paper was to assess the extent of application of WLC in the Public Terriary Education Building Projects (PTEBPs) in Yobe State. This study opted for quantitative research method. Survey questionnaire was used as an instrument for data collection. A total of 118 questionnaires were sent to construction practitioners in PTEBPs who work in clients', contractors' and consultants' organizations. These includes Quantity Surveyors, Architects and Engineers. The data collected were analysed using Relative Importance Index (RII), and One Way Analysis of Variance. The data analyis revealed that the extent of application of WLC in the study area was average (59.19%). The WLC elements that were highly considered at the early stage of project development include construction works cost, inflation, land acquisition and associated cost, design cost, statutory charges, energy consumption cost, maintenance cost, site costs and professional fees. The paper recommends that, relevant professional bodies such as Nigerian Institute of Quantity Surveyors should organize awareness workshop and training of construction professionals on the technique of WLC Analysis. This study can promote the implementation of WLC in public tertiary institutions in Nigeria.

papers.title: Assessing the implementation level of social procurement amongst Quantity Surveyors
papers.authors: BinUmar, Al-Amin Yakubu and Nasir, Rashida Maiturare
papers.abstract: Social procurement in construction addresses critical issues such as social disadvantage, economic challenges faced by Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), local economic development, and the promotion of sustainable business practices. The relational nature of social procurement policies requires construction firms to establish collaborative partnerships with government agencies, non-profit organisations, and community groups. Although this approach has gained global recognition, its adoption remains limited, particularly in developing countries. This study investigates the implementation of social procurement practices within the Nigerian construction industry. Data were collected via a questionnaire survey distributed to quantity surveyors in consultancy and contracting firms across Nigeria, achieving a response rate of 43%. The findings reveal that engaging local community stakeholders to understand their needs and incorporating these into procurement strategies is the most widely implemented social procurement practice. Conversely, practices such as supplier diversity programs encouraging participation from minority-owned and underrepresented businesses, supporting enterprises with a primary social mission (e.g., employing marginalized individuals), and providing training and support to disadvantaged suppliers to meet procurement requirements are among the least implemented. The study also highlights that while most respondents are aware of social procurement practices, their implementation remains significantly low in Nigeria. A key limitation of this research is its focus solely on quantity surveyors, suggesting that involving other stakeholders in future studies could provide a more comprehensive understanding. To enhance the implementation of social procurement practices in Nigeria, the study recommends awareness campaigns, stakeholder engagement initiatives, and robust policy development for social procurement.

papers.title: Comparative study of risk management capabilities of public and private parties in build-operate-transfer highway projects in Nigeria
papers.authors: Jonathan Kehinde Fabi and Olubola Atanda Akinseinde
papers.abstract: Risks inherent in highway construction projects using build-operate-transfer (BOT) approach are massive since there are numerous participants and agreements involved. To make sure risks are appropriately and sufficiently handled, there is urgent need to evaluate the parties' risk management capabilities in BOT highway projects. Therefore, this study evaluated and compared risk management capabilities (RMC) of public and private parties. A questionnaire survey was employed in this study to gather data from specialists involved in the building of BOT highways in Nigeria. Government representatives, highway engineers, concessionaires, quantity surveyors, bankers, contractors and academics make up the study's population. Stratified random sampling was used in the investigation. One hundred ten (110) questionnaires were distributed, and seventy-two (72) responses were received. Considering the multi-criteria problems to be solved, the study used the fuzzy synthetic evaluation (FSE) method to analyze the data. The findings showed that the RMC for culture and awareness of private sector participants, risk management practice and application, risk management resources, and risk management process are at managed level while that of public sector is at novice level. This indicates that private sector participants have more capability to manage risk than public sector participants. This study is very timely as it established the level at which each party has capability to manage risk in construction project. The two parties' risk management attribute requires further improvement to operate at 'optimized' risk management attribute so that risks in a project are allocated to the party who has the capability to manage it at minimum cost.

papers.title: Exploring the challenges and their implications on housing corporations' successful delivery of mass housing programme
papers.authors: Mansir Dodo, Rilwan Shuaib Abdulrahman, Ziyadul Hassan Ishaq and Ahmed Doko Ibrahim
papers.abstract: Nigeria has implemented numerous housing policies and programs with ambitious targets, yet the country continues to face a significant housing deficit. Historical evidence highlights consistent underperformance in mass housing programs (MHPs). Research emphasizes the critical role of Housing Corporations' (HCs) capacity in achieving housing policy goals. While studies indicate that HCs in North West Nigeria possess the potential to deliver MHPs successfully, they often overlook the vulnerabilities these corporations face. This study addresses that gap by exploring the challenges HCs encounter in delivering MHPs. A qualitative research approach was adopted, involving structured interviews with senior HC staff in North West Nigeria. Using an embedded multiple-case study method, respondents described their challenges within specific analytical units. Data were recorded, transcribed, screened, and analyzed through content analysis both within and across cases. Findings reveal that HCs face numerous challenges, including issues related to land ownership, project planning, construction, financing, and the sale or leasing of housing units. Key challenges include delays from authorities, inadequate funding, political interference, and high costs of building materials. The study concludes that addressing these challenges is crucial for MHP success and recommends strategic interventions to mitigate vulnerabilities. Future research should examine HCs in other region to provide a comprehensive understanding of these challenges worldwide.

papers.title: Categorisation of prudence practice in construction project management in Lagos State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Morakinyo, A., Onabanjo, A. A., Akeredolu, T. B. and Yohanna, H. S
papers.abstract: Prudence refers to using a certain amount of judiciousness when establishing estimates under uncertain circumstances so that resources, income, or liabilities are not overstated or understated. The cardinal constraints of budget, duration, and quality are ever-present in construction project delivery. Managers of construction project can benefit from relevant prudence practice applicable to other investments. In order to prevent re-inventing the engine, the managers categorisation is important to highlight prudence practice in other investment that will improve construction project performance. However, the adoption and extension of prudence practice of other sectors to construction project management are scanty in the literature. Therefore, this study aims to empirically categorise the prudence practices (PP) in the management of construction projects in Lagos State, Nigeria. In no particular order, 27 prudence practice variants were assessed through quantitative study. A response rate of 86.67 percent was achieved from 150 questionnaires self-administered on construction sector professionals. However, 6.15 percent of the retrieved questionnaires were excluded during SPSS (V.29) statistical analysis. A major result from the classification of the prudence practice of project managers on construction projects indicated that the current prudence is relatively adequate to implement the construction objectives of the client in terms of budget and completion date. In conclusion, project managers are yet to attain the very desirable prudence practices in terms of being “Highly and Very Highly prudence, which are the ultimate. This deficiency would impact the value on investment on construction project. Therefore, further studies will be needed to estimate such impact.

papers.title: Towards successful e-tendering: examining barriers, benefits and success factors for Nigerian construction firms
papers.authors: Yazeed Yakubu
papers.abstract: Electronic Tendering is an agent of change and game changer that is shaping the direction of construction procurement in this modern world. The study aimed at measuring the capacity of contracting firms in e-tendering adoption by identifying the key enablers and bottlenecks, the research seeks to provide actionable insight for stakeholders to enhance digital adoption in the construction industry thereby speeding up their tendering processes for improved project delivery. The study employed quantitative approach and data for the study was gathered using a structured questionnaire, a convenience sampling technique was used and distributed 20 questionnaires to 20 firms. The study used percentages and relative importance index in ranking the factors. It has however, been concluded that contracting firms in Katsina metropolis are aware of the technology and ready to adopt e-tendering systems. This was informed by the responses of the participants. The study however, recommends that; Government should incentivize the use of e-tendering by firms; Professional bodies such NIQS at state and national levels to be organizing more workshops and training on e-tendering; Accredited Institutions offering Quantity Surveying courses should include e-tendering as part of its curriculum; More public awareness be carried out by professional bodies and the academia to convince private clients and government to embrace e-tendering.

papers.title: An evaluation of carbon costing education among Nigerian Quantity Surveyors
papers.authors: Ibrahim Sha'aba, Dr. Olusola Ogunsina and Dr. Christianah Adah
papers.abstract: The construction industry is a major contributor to global carbon emissions, with quantity surveyors (QSs) increasingly expected to integrate carbon management into cost planning. This study evaluates the state of carbon costing education among Nigerian QSs, focusing on the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). A mixed-methods approach was adopted, combining questionnaire responses from 94 registered QSs, document analysis of university curricula, and semi-structured interviews with professionals holding sustainability certifications. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and reliability measures were used to analyze quantitative data, while Saldaña's coding method supported qualitative analysis. Findings indicate that although sustainability awareness is relatively high, proper knowledge and practical exposure to carbon costing remain low. Over half of the respondents exhibited “false awareness”—defined as recognizing carbon costing terminology without corresponding understanding or application. University curricula offered minimal content on life cycle assessment (LCA) and embodied carbon, whereas NIQS workshops and CPD programs focused on general sustainability themes rather than technical carbon costing issues. The evidence validates the hypothesis that awareness and knowledge of carbon costing among Nigerian QSs are limited. The study recommends curriculum reforms, integration of carbon-related CPD requirement, and stronger policy alignment to bridge the education- practice gap.

papers.title: Factors influencing the adoption of corporate social responsibility for the delivery of infrastructural projects in Lagos State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Oluwaseyi Olalekan Alao, Nofiu Abiodun Musa and Mujidat Olubola Babalola
papers.abstract: Integrating corporate social responsibility into financing of infrastructural projects is still evolving in Nigeria. This study investigated the factors influencing the involvement of private organisations in the delivery of CSR-based infrastructural projects with a view to enhancing their optimum participation, and framework development. Primary data for the study were collected using a structured questionnaire and semi-structured interviews. The questionnaire was administered on 27 representatives who had been involved in the administration of CSR in the private organisations that were identified through Respondents-Driven Sampling (RDS) technique. In addition, nine of these representatives were selected for interviews using convenience/accidental sampling technique. The data collected were analyzed using mean analysis, Kruskal-Wallis test, and thematic analysis. The findings showed that the significant factor influencing organisations' involvement in the delivery of CSR-based infrastructural projects were increased image and reputation of the firms, public relations, commitment to environmental sustainability, ethical, moral and personal value of the management, and compliance with international standardistaion. The study concluded that CSR activities of the private organisations in Lagos State were those commensurate with their economic performance and are capable of impacting their performance when executed. It is recommended that the public sector should leverage the strength of the private sector organizations for improved involvement in the delivery of infrastructure project.

papers.title: E-Communication risk in public private partnership project in Nigeria
papers.authors: Yazeed Yakubu and Yazid Ibrahim Muhammed
papers.abstract: Communication is an important ingredient that's underpinning the performance of organizations. This study is aimed at creating awareness on the emerging risk of e-communication in public private partnership in Nigeria, with special emphasis on concession arrangements in Katsina state. The study employed a quantitative approach and data for the study was collected using a structured questionnaire. The target respondent for the study were consultants (in both private and public) and Contractors. The study distributed 65 questionnaires using convenience sampling and recorded a response rate of 76.92% (50). The study however, indicated that the frequency of e-communication in PPP projects was very frequent which recorded a total of 40% and 86% of the respondents prefer e-communication and paperless. While the type of e-equipment used for communication were telephone (44%) and e-mail (30%). The reasons given by the respondents for opting for phone and e-mail were ease of use, been faster and cheap. About 90% of the respondent encountered problem with the equipment used. However, the problems encountered in e-communication using phone and e-mail were unstructured information (44%), insecurity of the channel (32%) and insufficient bandwidth and network (24%) among other factors. The study recommends among others that seminars and symposia be organized to train and retrain experts on the use of e-devices in a PPP project; standard mean of sending e-information should be devised to regulate communication between parties in a concession arrangement; genuine internet and mobile service providers should be identified and protonized for communication in PPP projects.

papers.title: Assessment of cultural barriers to the implementation of building information modelling (BIM) in the nigerian construction industry
papers.authors: Nathaniel Sankun Bunchang-Terra, Saidu Minin Mohammed and Hassan Adaviriku Ahmadu
papers.abstract: Building Information Modelling (BIM) has become a cornerstone of digital transformation in construction globally, offering integrated project planning, coordination, and lifecycle optimisation. Despite its global success in improving efficiency, sustainability, and collaboration, adoption in Nigeria remains slow and fragmented, with cultural barriers exerting as significant an influence as technical or financial limitations. This study identifies and ranks nineteen key cultural impediments, including resistance to change, hierarchical decision-making, lack of trust, and perceptions of BIM as a “Western” technology, amongst others. A quantitative survey was conducted by distributing 172 copies of structured questionnaires to construction professionals, yielding 106 valid responses that were analysed using SPSS. Descriptive statistics and exploratory factor analysis provided insights into critical challenges. Results reveal that client conservatism or lack of awareness of BIM, resistance to change from 2D/CAD workflows, and the perceived complexity of BIM processes are the top-ranked barriers. These challenges cluster into two overarching dimensions: Organisational and Operational Resistance; and Socio-Cultural and Policy Barriers. The findings highlight that BIM adoption in Nigeria is not only a technical issue but a cultural transformation requiring leadership commitment, policy reform, and stakeholder collaboration. The study recommends government-led mandates, context-specific localisation strategies, targeted professional training, and structured change management. These interventions are essential for aligning Nigeria's construction industry with global best practices. This research fills a critical gap by foregrounding culture, not just technology or finance as the linchpin of successful BIM adoption in Nigeria.

papers.title: The evolving roles of quantity surveyors in sustainable construction project delivery
papers.authors: Jobin Ishaya
papers.abstract: The growing demand for sustainable construction presents new opportunities and responsibilities for Quantity Surveyors (QS) globally. This study examines the evolving roles of Quantity Surveyors in delivering sustainable construction projects and highlights how these roles can be integrated into global QS practice. Using a quantitative research approach, data were collected from 76 Quantity Surveyors across four continents through an online questionnaire. Descriptive statistical analysis using SPSS revealed that Quantity Surveyors play critical roles in sustainability strategy development, energy efficiency advisory, green financing, life-cycle costing, and consulting on sustainable materials. Findings indicate that QS professionals are expanding beyond traditional cost management to include environmental and social sustainability considerations in project delivery. The study concludes that Quantity Surveyors must strengthen their sustainability competencies to remain key contributors to achieving the United Nations' sustainable development goals in the built environment. It is recommended that Quantity Surveyors enhance their competencies in sustainability assessment, energy modelling, and life-cycle analysis. Professional institutions should provide targeted training and encourage sustainability-driven practice to ensure the continued relevance of the profession in the evolving built environment.

papers.title: An assessment of building and engineering standard method of measurement4 adoption of by Quantity Surveyors in Ondo State, Nigeria
papers.authors: Kehinde Wiston Olayinka and Olubunmi Comfort Ade-Ojo
papers.abstract: The construction industry in Nigeria faces challenges that impact construction standards, partly due to inconsistent adoption of specifications, standards, and regulations. The study assessed the level of adoption of Building and Engineering Standard Method of Measurement 4 (BESMM4) by Quantity Surveyors in preparing Bills of Quantities (BOQs) in Ondo State, Nigeria. It assessed problems associated with using the Building and Engineering Standard Method of Measurement 4, and the factors inhibiting its adoption by Quantity Surveyors. The methodology included the use of questionnaires administered to Quantity Surveyors in Akure, Ondo State. A purposive sampling of registered quantity Surveyors in Ondo state was conducted. The data collected were subjected to statistical analysis. The result showed that the Quantity Surveyors have not been adequately utilizing the current BESMM4. The major factor inhibiting its adoption is the level of familiarity with BESMM4, while the major problem identified with the use of the BESMM4 was with Heavy Engineering Works. In conclusion, the BESMM4 is relevant to the quantity surveying profession, but its adoption is hindered by various factors. The study recommends that the Nigerian Institute of Quantity Surveyors (NIQS) should organize more workshops to educate quantity surveyors on the use and benefits of BESMM4, especially for heavy engineering works, and promote the adoption of BESMM4 as a standard for preparing tenders and encourage quantity surveyors and firms to embrace its use. In conclusion, Quantity Surveyors should do more by adopting the current form of Standard Method of Measurement (BESMM4).

papers.title: Earned and expended man-hours based lost productivity prediction in =[ construction projects: a recurrent neural network (RNN) model for sustainable resource management and optimization
papers.authors: Samuel I. Egwunatum, Mercyjane N. Ihekweme, Benjamin E. Idisi and Opeyemi A. Osadola
papers.abstract: Construction projects frequently experience lost productivity, resulting in claims and strained project management. This study investigates the application of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) analysis in predicting lost productivity using historical earned and expended man-hours data. A comprehensive dataset of 105 work items, estimated using the Moselhi et al. methodology, was provided by industry experts. The RNN model, leveraging Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), was optimized through backpropagation and hyperparameter tuning. The results demonstrate impressive predictive capabilities, with a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 14.58, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 3.82, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 3.05, and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 33.52. These findings suggest that the RNN model can accurately forecast lost productivity, enabling proactive measures to mitigate delays and cost overruns. The model's performance was validated through real-time sequence construction jobs, demonstrating its suitability for assessing lost labor values in building projects. This study provides a practical tool for construction professionals to counter claims, disputes, and demands.

papers.title: Modelling the influence of public procurement success factors on challenges and performance: a quantitative analysis from Kaduna state, Nigeria
papers.authors: Buba Gumgaro Simon-Peter, Yohanna Bareh Galadima, Paul Naomi Bala, and Ishaya Jobin
papers.abstract: Public procurement plays a crucial role in ensuring transparency, accountability, and efficiency in the delivery of public sector projects. Despite the enactment of Nigeria's Public Procurement Act (2007), persistent issues such as inflated contract costs, poor budgetary provisions, weak institutional structures, and limited political will continue to hinder its effectiveness. This study establishes the relationship between the success factors, challenges, and the extent of improvement (performance) of the public procurement in Kaduna state. A quantitative research design was adopted, employing a structured questionnaire administered to 185 procurement personnel across ministries, agencies, and the Kaduna State Public Procurement Authority. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. Findings reveal that success factors significantly and positively influence both procurement challenges (β = 0.406, p < 0.01) and performance (β = 0.192, p > 0.05), with a more substantial effect on challenges, indicating that systemic obstacles remain a dominant barrier to optimal performance. The results underscore the need for government and regulatory bodies to strengthen institutional frameworks, enforce anti-corruption measures, and improve budgetary planning to reduce procurement inefficiencies. By addressing these challenges, Kaduna State can enhance transparency, competitiveness, and value-for-money in public procurement, thereby improving project outcomes and fostering sustainable development.

papers.title: Effect of geotechnical factors on building construction cost in Akwa Ibom State
papers.authors: Christian Asuquo, Samuel Ekung and Daniel Oghumu
papers.abstract: The influence of geotechnical conditions on construction outcomes remains a central theme in foundation engineering and site development. This study examined the effect of geotechnical factors on building construction cost in Akwa Ibom State. Cost information on building substructure were obtained from priced Bills of Quantities (BOQs) of 15 two-storey buildings recently completed. In addition, a well-structured questionnaire was used to generate responses from 155 construction professionals comprising civil engineers, quantity surveyors, architects, and builders. Mean item scores and Spearman rank order correlation were used in analysing the data. The results revealed that the most critical geotechnical factors influencing building costs are groundwater table levels, soil bearing capacity and groundwater conditions. The analysis of the BOQs revealed that substructure works accounted for average of 19.90% of total building costs. The results of the Spearman correlation revealed a strong positive and significant correlation between variable subsurface condition (r = 0.812; p < 0.01), soil bearing capacity (r = 0.801; p < 0.05) and groundwater conditions (r = 0.795; p < 0.01) and substructure cost. It was concluded that a wide range of geotechnical factors influence construction costs in Akwa Ibom state. However, rock presence and obstruction does not have a significant relationship with cost of substructure. It is recommended that project teams should conduct comprehensive site investigations, select site-specific foundation designs, implement ground improvement techniques, incorporate groundwater management and dewatering strategies and integrate probabilistic risk assessment when budgeting for building projects.

papers.title: Ethical challenges in quantity surveying and their impact on project cost in Port Harcourt metropolis
papers.authors: Kelechi Godson and Alolote Ibim Amadi
papers.abstract: The construction sector in Port Harcourt, Nigeria, continues to grapple with significant ethical issues that adversely influence project outcomes, particularly in the area of cost management. Quantity surveyors-play a vital role in overseeing and controlling project costs, yet they often face ethical dilemmas that hinder the effective execution of construction projects. This study examined the ethical challenges faced by quantity surveyors and their impact on project cost in Port Harcourt Metropolis. A descriptive survey research design was adopted, utilizing structured five-Point Likert-scale questionnaires administered to various construction stakeholders such as quantity surveyors, engineers, project managers, and contractors within the Port Harcourt Metropolis. The study adopted a purposive sampling technique. Out of one hundred and eleven (111) questionnaires distributed to various respondents, eighty seven (87) were retrieved and found valid for the data analysis. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, including mean scores and standard deviations. The findings indicated that the most prevalent ethical problems include bribery and corruption, prevalence of inflated variation order, falsification of bills of quantities, and lack of whistleblower protection. These unethical practices were attributed to inadequate institutional regulation, low professional remuneration, weak monitoring systems, and intense socio-economic pressures within the rapidly expanding construction industry in Port Harcourt. Consequently, the study recommends that Professional bodies such as Nigerian Institute of Quantity Surveyors (NIQS) and the Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria (QSRBN) should establish comprehensive ethical monitoring systems capable of identifying, documenting, and tracking patterns of unethical conduct-including falsification of cost information, bid manipulation, bribery, and collusive practices.

papers.title: Climate resilience measures of buildings along Lagos coastlines: professional awareness and lifecycle integration
papers.authors: Olusegun Akinsiku, Omotayo Gbolahan and Mobolaji Oluwadiya
papers.abstract: Buildings in coastal areas are usually exposed to severe climate risks that threaten their performance and sustainability. Mitigation strategies to address the impacts of climate change and global warming remain heterogeneous, especially in developing countries of the global south. This study examines the gap between professional knowledge and on-site implementation of climate resilience in the management of construction projects along coastal lines, using buildings in the Lekki area of Lagos state, Nigeria, as a case study. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey using purposive sampling was carried out among 200 construction professionals, including project managers, engineers, architects, builders, quantity surveyors and facility managers. Descriptive statistics were used to assess respondents' awareness of key attributes of building resilience and to analyse the extent to which resilience is considered across the project's phases. A cross-tabulation chisquare and one-way ANOVA tests examined whether resilience awareness differs significantly across professional groups within the construction industry. The findings show moderate to high levels of awareness of climate risks and resilience principles, particularly robustness, recovery, and adaptability. The findings revealed that the difference in awareness scores among the six professional groups is not statistically significant. It was equally found that the integration of resilience by professionals is concentrated during the planning and design phases; however, this wanes during the execution, handover and post-construction phases. Implementation is mainly characterised by the use of conventional engineering measures, while strategies based on redundancy and nature remain marginal. The study concludes that the main barrier to coastal construction is not a lack of awareness but the failure of current project delivery systems to maintain the resilience intent throughout a project's life cycle. These findings highlight the need for lifecycle-oriented incorporation of resilience, focused capacity building, and strengthening of institutional guidance to improve the climate resilience of coastal construction in fast-urbanising cities like Lagos.

papers.title: A study of safety management in the construction industry in Nigeria, Ogun State as a case study
papers.authors: Oladosu Oluwatobiloba Adedayo
papers.abstract: The construction industry in Ogun State, Nigeria, faces persistent safety challenges, including weak compliance with safety procedures, poor regulatory enforcement, and frequent workplace accidents. This study examined the effect of safety management practices on construction safety performance in Ogun State, focusing on safety training and education, policy implementation and enforcement, and safety monitoring and supervision. A descriptive survey design was adopted. Using stratified random sampling, data were collected from construction professionals and artisans across the three senatorial districts of Ogun State. Of 200 questionnaires administered, 187 valid responses were analysed, representing a 93.5% response rate. Data were gathered through a structured questionnaire with a Cronbach's Alpha of 0.84. Descriptive statistics, including frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviations, were used to summarise the data, while multiple regression analysis tested the hypotheses at the 0.05 significance level. The findings showed that safety training and education significantly improved workers' compliance and reduced accident rates (R = 0.782, R² = 0.611, F = 129.876, p < 0.05). Policy implementation and enforcement also had a significant positive effect on safety performance (R = 0.756, R² = 0.571, F = 113.935, p < 0.05). Safety monitoring and supervision likewise significantly improved risk reduction and maintenance of safety standards (R = 0.741, R² = 0.549, F = 107.631, p < 0.05). The study concluded that effective safety management practices are essential for improving safety performance and reducing construction risks in Ogun State. It recommended continuous worker training, stricter enforcement of safety regulations, and stronger site supervision.

papers.title: Evaluating the regulatory efficacy of Nigeria's national blockchain policy in promoting public procurement transparency
papers.authors: Nuhu Jega Abdullahi, Muhammad Abdullahi and Abdulganiyu Adebayo Oke
papers.abstract: Public procurement systems in many emerging economies continue to face persistent challenges of opacity, discretionary decision-making, and weak institutional accountability. These challenges are particularly pronounced within the construction sector, where large public expenditures and complex contracting processes often create opportunities for inefficiency and corruption. In response to these governance concerns, the Federal Government of Nigeria introduced the National Blockchain Policy (NBP) in 2023 as part of a broader digital governance reform agenda aimed at improving transparency, traceability, and trust in public sector transactions. Despite the growing global interest in blockchain-enabled governance, limited empirical research has examined the regulatory effectiveness of national blockchain policies in addressing procurement transparency challenges. This study, therefore, evaluates the regulatory efficacy of the NBP in promoting transparency within Nigeria's construction procurement system. Guided by Institutional Theory, the research adopts a mixed-methods design that integrates policy content analysis, a structured survey of 215 procurement professionals, and semi-structured interviews with 15 experts in procurement governance, blockchain technology, and regulatory practice. The findings reveal a pronounced regulatory paradox: while the NBP is widely perceived as a transformative policy capable of strengthening transparency and accountability, its practical implementation is constrained by regulatory ambiguity, institutional inertia, and limited technical capacity. The study highlights a persistent disconnect between policy ambition and operational enforcement. By providing empirical insights into the institutional dynamics shaping digital governance reforms, this research contributes to emerging scholarship on blockchain-enabled public procurement and offers policy-relevant guidance for strengthening transparency oriented regulatory frameworks in Nigeria and other emerging economies.

papers.title: Assessment of the impact of blockchain technology on transparency in e-procurement: a comparative analysis
papers.authors: Saidu Minin Mohammed, Ismail Sukaraju Ahamad, Hassan Adaviriku Ahmadu, and Mohammed Abdullahi
papers.abstract: This study assesses the perceived impact of blockchain technology on enhancing transparency in e-procurement, comparing blockchain-based systems with traditional e-procurement platforms within the context of the Nigerian construction industry. A quantitative research design was employed, utilising a structured questionnaire distributed to 172 construction professionals, including architects, builders, engineers, quantity surveyors, and procurement officers, using purposive sampling. A total of 79 valid responses were received. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Exploratory Factor Analysis, and paired samples t-tests via SPSS v27 to compare transparency indicators between the two systems. The findings reveal significant transparency deficiencies in traditional e-procurement systems, including susceptibility to data manipulation, weak audit trails, and limited stakeholder access. In contrast, blockchain-based e-procurement was perceived to offer statistically significant advantages (p < 0.05) across all measured indicators: higher transparency levels (Cohen's d = 0.87), greater stakeholder trust (d = 0.40), improved auditability (d = 0.27), lower record tampering risk (d = 0.25), and reduced manipulation risk (d = 0.50). Exploratory factor analysis identified two principal components explaining 72% of the variance, distinguishing blockchain's enabling features from traditional systems' challenges. The study provides empirical evidence supporting the strategic adoption of blockchain to mitigate corruption and enhance accountability in public and private sector procurement. Recommendations include stakeholder training, supportive policy frameworks, pilot implementations, and infrastructural upgrades. This research contributes to the nascent body of knowledge on blockchain in procurement by providing comparative, context-specific empirical evidence from a developing economy, addressing a significant gap in the literature where such studies are scarce.

papers.title: Barriers to successful implementation of waste management strategies in sustainable construction projects in Lagos, Nigeria
papers.authors: Femi Philip Olorundare, Abdulhammed Adebisi Sotomiwa and Yisah Emmanuella Ohunene
papers.abstract: In Lagos, Nigeria, sustainable projects face enormous environmental and resource issues due to rapid urbanization and intensive construction and demolition (C&D) waste. This study identifies and ranks barriers to implementing waste management strategies in sustainable construction in Lagos. A quantitative survey using a structured questionnaire was conducted on 109 construction professionals (stratified random sampling based on NIQS, NIA, NSE, and NIOB registers). 88 valid responses were received (80.73% response rate). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics (Mean Item Score and standard deviation) and inferential factor analysis (SPSS). The top barriers included a lack of awareness and training (MIS = 4.35), inadequate planning (4.20), and poor regulatory enforcement (4.08). Factor analysis grouped the barriers into four factors with Cronbach's alpha values of 0.812–0.915. Recommendations include enhanced training, strict enforcement, mandatory waste plans, and incentives to SMEs to help improve sustainable practices and minimize environmental impact. This study offers empirical evidence on Lagos-specific barriers to sustainable construction that contribute to the localized studies on sustainable construction in Nigeria.

papers.title: A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of sustainable procurement in developing countries
papers.authors: Usman Sulaiman Jibril, Muhammad Abdullahi, Rilwan Shuaib Abdulrahman, and Rashida Maiturare Nasir
papers.abstract: Sustainable procurement is increasingly recognised as a strategic tool for promoting environmental, social, and economic objectives, particularly within the construction sector in developing countries. Despite its significance, the practical adoption of sustainable procurement in these contexts remains limited due to institutional, financial, and technological challenges. This study conducts a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis on sustainable procurement practices in developing nations between 2000 and 2024. Adata set of 41 articles retrieved from OpenAlex and Scopus database were analysed using VOSViewer to identify dominant themes, research trends, enablers, and barriers. Findings highlighted that environmental criteria are most commonly emphasised, often overshadowing social and economic dimensions. Initiatives such as the integration of life cycle costing, CO₂ emission assessments, and digital innovations like blockchain have been proposed to enhance transparency and efficiency in procurement processes. However, challenges such as lack of regulatory enforcement, limited professional capacity, and weak market readiness persist. Furthermore, bibliometric analysis reveals a concentration of research within a few institutions and limited cross-national collaboration, underscoring the need for broader stakeholder engagement. The study suggests that developing countries should strengthen legal frameworks, invest in capacity building for procurement professionals, and adopt digital tools to improve accountability and environmental performance. Greater emphasis on social sustainability, such as community engagement, local employment, and ethical standards, is recommended to achieve more holistic procurement outcomes. This study contributes to bridging the knowledge gap by providing an updated synthesis of theoretical and empirical insights, offering actionable recommendations for policymakers and practitioners aiming to advance sustainable procurement in developing contexts.

papers.title: An exploration of BIM-enabled circular procurement for sustainable construction
papers.authors: Alice Ogunlolu, Blessing Okosun, Chioma Precious Ekweani and Saidu Minin Mohammed
papers.abstract: The construction industry faces increasing pressure to adopt sustainable and resource-efficient practices that support circular economy (CE) objectives and net-zero targets. Building Information Modelling (BIM) has emerged as a key digital technology capable of enhancing lifecycle decision-making; however, its role in enabling circular procurement during the pre-construction phase remains underexplored. This study investigates how BIM and CE principles can be integrated within pre-construction procurement processes to improve sustainability outcomes in the UK Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) sector. Using an interpretivist qualitative approach, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with industry professionals involved in procurement, design, project management and digital construction. The data were analysed using thematic analysis to identify the key opportunities, barriers and enablers associated with BIM-enabled circular procurement. The findings indicate that BIM can facilitate CE implementation through improved material traceability, lifecycle assessment, digital material passports, enhanced stakeholder collaboration and data-driven procurement decisions. However, adoption remains hindered by organizational capability gaps, fragmented procurement practices, interoperability challenges, limited knowledge of circular economy principles and inconsistent policy support. The study further identifies lifecycle-based procurement, early stakeholder engagement, standardized BIM-CE frameworks, stronger regulatory mechanisms and targeted professional training as critical factors for successful implementation. By demonstrating how digital technologies and circular economy principles can be strategically aligned during the pre-construction stage, this research contributes to the sustainable procurement literature and provides practical insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders seeking to accelerate the transition towards a more resource-efficient, low-carbon and resilient construction sector.

papers.title: Adoption and sustainability of donor-funded higher education buildings in Nigeria: A review of impact of its influencing factors
papers.authors: Adepoju Moses Adejumo and Temilola Mopelola Adejumo
papers.abstract: There has been a general increase in the decadence and lack of facilities and infrastructure required to meet the needs of students and lecturers in the higher education system, prompting stakeholders and individuals to fund and donate building infrastructure to counter the government's low funding of the system. This review investigates the impact of factors influencing the adoption of donor-funded buildings in the Nigerian higher education system, with the goal of evaluating education funding over the last 25 years and proposing a better mechanism for scaling up infrastructure provision in the Nigerian higher education system. The paper used a comprehensive search of scholarly sources to identify 65 publications that were reviewed by title, abstract, and full text to resolve similarities, out of which 44 publications met the criteria, and were screened using inclusion and exclusion criteria, and analyzed using thematic synthesis. It was found that five major influencing factors impacting donor-funded building adoption in the Nigerian higher education system are government policy and regulatory environment. This study also discovered that the adoption and sustainability of donor-funded building projects are dependent on these influencing factors. The study indicated that the Nigerian government underfunds educational infrastructure in higher education, and that the adoption of donor-funded projects is low due to its reliance on significant influencing factors. As a result, higher education institutions and associated authorities should strengthen planning and accountability, processes, managerial and technical capability, and provide clear maintenance frameworks to facilitate adoption.

papers.title: Future proofing infrastructure planning and development in Nigeria: The convergence and cost management benefits of construction 4.0 technologies
papers.authors: Alolote Amadi Ibim
papers.abstract: A key feature of modern futuristic infrastructure development is the convergence of data driven Construction 4.0 technologies, which foster more intelligent and interconnected systems as a strategic imperative for improving infrastructure planning, delivery, and cost management. However, the adoption and integration of Construction 4.0 technologies remain limited in Nigeria, resulting in persistent project cost overruns, delays, resource inefficiencies, and poor lifecycle asset performance. This study investigates the influence of Construction 4.0 technologies such as Building Information Modelling (BIM), Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and Digital Twins on infrastructure cost management in Nigeria's infrastructure planning and development. A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured questionnaire administered through purposive sampling to construction professionals. A total of 291 valid responses were analysed using descriptive statistics, Relative Importance Index (RII), correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The findings reveal that Building Information Modelling is the most influential Construction 4.0 technology, followed by Artificial Intelligence, the Internet of Things, and Digital Twins. The regression model was statistically significant (F = 147.86, p < 0.001) and explained 67.4% of the variation in infrastructure cost management (R² = 0.674), confirming that the integrated adoption of Construction 4.0 technologies significantly improves cost forecasting, budget accuracy, resource optimisation, reduction of rework and material waste, project delivery, and lifecycle cost performance. The study submits that by leveraging the tools of construction 4.0, Nigeria has the futuristic capacity to fundamentally reshape and minimise the cost of infrastructure development, transmuting from a constraint on growth into a resilient backbone for transformative national development.

papers.title: Construction finance professionals' perceptions of traditional and activity-based costing techniques for enhancing construction company profitability in Nigeria
papers.authors: Ariba Isaac Robinson
papers.abstract: The study examined construction finance professionals' perceptions of traditional and activity based costing techniques for enhancing construction company profitability in Nigeria. Two research hypotheses in line with purpose of the study were formulated and anchored on establishing significant relationships between use of both Traditional Costing Technique (TCT) and Activity Based Costing (ABC), and enhancement of construction project profitability. A survey research design was adopted by the study using questionnaire comprising two research questions with 38 researcher formulated multiple choice items. Sample size of 385 respondents was selected from the population based on Cochran's sample size formula. A four-point Likert Scale was used in the study. The data collected for the study were analyzed using weighted mean and standard deviation. Demographics of the respondents were subjected to Chi-square which made their data categorized. The reliability scale was measured using Cronbach's alpha, Guttman's lambda and corrected item–total correlation range while the hypotheses were tested using Confirmatory Factor Analysis and Structural Equation Model. The respondents overwhelmingly rejected the view that costing techniques fail to enhance profitability in construction companies. The study found that TCT had a significant positive effect on profitability (β = 0.337, p<0.05) while ABC also had a significant positive effect on profitability (β =0.389, p<0.001). The study among others recommended use of traditional costing techniques and activity based costing techniques as complements in a hybrid arrangement, use of TCT for internal financial reporting and ABC for external users of data from construction companies in Nigeria.

papers.title: Integrating sustainability into construction: The strategic role of quantity surveyors in material selection
papers.authors: Ayobami Oluwaseun Idowu and Gabriel Sanni
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for environmentally responsible construction has positioned sustainability as a critical priority within the built environment. This study examines the strategic role of quantity surveyors in integrating sustainability into construction through effective material selection. Quantity surveyors are increasingly expected to incorporate environmental and social considerations into their professional practices. The study investigates how their expertise in cost planning, procurement, and lifecycle costing can support the adoption of sustainable materials without compromising project viability. A quantitative research approach was adopted, utilizing a structured questionnaire administered to among quantity surveyors in Edo State, Nigeria. A total of 85 questionnaires were administered and 80 were returned and considered fit for analysis. Data was analyzed using descriptive statistics to identify key factors influencing sustainable material selection and the extent of quantity surveyors' involvement. The findings reveal that quantity surveyors play a pivotal role in evaluating material costs over the project lifecycle, advising on alternatives with lower environmental impact, and ensuring compliance with sustainability standards. However, challenges such as limited knowledge of green materials, lack of standardized guidelines, and cost constraints were identified as barriers to effective integration. The study concludes that quantity surveyors are essential drivers of sustainable construction, particularly in bridging the gap between economic feasibility and environmental performance. It recommends continuous professional development and training for quantity surveyors to enhance technical competence in sustainable construction practices. This research contributes to the growing body of knowledge on sustainable construction and highlights the need for a multidisciplinary approach to achieving long-term environmental goals in the construction industry.

papers.title: Exploring the determinants of blockchain technology integration in emerging markets: An empirical study of Nigerian construction sector
papers.authors: Akinrata Ebunoluwa Bimbola, Ayodeji Emmanuel Oke and Olusile Adeolu Adewunmi
papers.abstract: Despite blockchain's potential to resolve endemic challenges including cost overruns, schedule delays, and supply chain fragmentation, adoption rates remain notably low in developing economies. Therefore, this study evaluates the determinants of blockchain technology (BcT) adoption in Nigeria's construction sector, addressing the critical gap between theoretical promise and practical implementation in emerging markets. Through a survey of 219 construction professionals, this research employed descriptive statistics and Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) to identify and categorize key adoption determinants. Twenty determinants were initially identified from the literature and subsequently analyzed using mean item scores and factor analysis. Results revealed that time management, company size, and human capital management constitute the most critical determinants, while type of company emerged as the least influential factor. The EFA extracted six principal components: intention to adopt and use BcT, nature of work, type of company, governance structure and blockchain vendor requirements, customer demand for blockchain, and efficiency and cost savings. However, current adoption levels remain predominantly low, with 56.2% of respondents rating adoption as low or very low. These findings provide empirical insights into blockchain adoption dynamics within resource-constrained environments and offer actionable guidance for stakeholders seeking to facilitate technological integration in emerging market construction sectors.

papers.title: Towards a cost-efficient transformation of Nigeria's public procurement processes: Examining stakeholders' perceptions of traditional versus integrated digital systems
papers.authors: Alolote Amadi Ibim
papers.abstract: Traditional public procurement systems in Nigeria are constrained by fragmented processes, limited transparency, and administrative inefficiencies, highlighting the need for digital transformation. This study comparatively evaluates the performance of traditional procurement systems and integrated digital procurement systems comprising Electronic Procurement (E-Procurement), Building Information Modelling (BIM), and Artificial Intelligence (AI). A quantitative comparative research design was adopted. Data were collected through structured questionnaires administered to public procurement stakeholders using purposive sampling, to select procurement professionals with relevant knowledge and experience in public procurement and digital procurement systems. A total of 186 valid responses were analysed using descriptive statistics, the Relative Importance Index (RII), and paired comparative statistical analysis. The findings indicate that integrated digital procurement systems are perceived to outperform traditional procurement systems in procurement speed, transparency, accountability, collaboration, data accessibility, decision-making quality, and perceived cost efficiency. Transparency improvement, faster procurement processes, and improved data management emerged as the most significant benefits of digital procurement integration. Respondents also perceived BIM as enhancing procurement coordination and lifecycle information management, while AI improves supplier evaluation, procurement intelligence, risk management, and automated contract administration. Statistical analysis confirmed a significant difference between stakeholders' perceptions of traditional and integrated digital procurement systems. However, implementation is constrained by inadequate ICT infrastructure, limited technical expertise, organisational resistance to change, and weak regulatory support. The study concludes that successful digital transformation of Nigeria's public procurement system requires integrated adoption of E-Procurement, BIM, and AI, supported by policy reforms, institutional capacity building, and sustained investment in digital infrastructure.

papers.title: Assessment of the barriers affecting the adoption of sustainable building materials (SBMs) for renovation projects
papers.authors: Saidu Minin Mohammed, Idris Musa Aliyu, and Alice Ogunlolu
papers.abstract: The building renovation sector is critical for achieving global energy and decarbonization targets. However, the adoption of Sustainable Building Materials (SBMs) in these projects, particularly in developing countries like Nigeria, faces significant impediments. While barriers to sustainable construction have been studied, the specific context of renovation projects remains underexplored. This study aims to identify and assess the critical barriers hindering the adoption of SBMs for building renovation projects within the Nigerian construction industry. A quantitative research approach was employed, utilising a structured questionnaire administered to 170 professionals (Quantity Surveyors, Architects, and Builders) selected via stratified random sampling. Data collected from 55 valid responses were analysed using descriptive statistics (mean score ranking) and inferential statistics. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) was used to identify the underlying dimensions of the identified barriers. The KMO measure was 0.791, indicating meritorious sampling adequacy. Bartlett's Test of Sphericity was significant (χ² = 1013.440, p < 0.001), confirming that the correlation matrix was appropriate for factor analysis. The Cronbach's Alpha was 0.937, indicating excellent internal consistency. The most significant barriers were found to be a lack of understanding of statutory requirements and policies; inadequate institutional structures at the local level; and a lack of strategy to promote sustainable construction. The adoption of SBMs in Nigerian renovation projects is primarily obstructed by systemic governmental, institutional, and policy-related failures rather than just high costs or material availability. Addressing these top-tier barriers through targeted policy formulation, institutional strengthening, and strategic promotion is essential for fostering a sustainable renovation market. MEDIA: []
